entries.title: Accessibility International
entries.description: Accessibility International is the agency that treats every information casualty like a plane crash, founded by a 2069 unit stranded in 2026.
entries.markdown: # Accessibility International > Accessibility International is the agency that treats every information casualty like a plane crash, founded by a 2069 unit stranded in 2026. **Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real. **Accessibility International** (AcsInt, or simply A.I.) is the institution that succeeds [Rungwell](https://charli.info/charlipedia/rungwell/) when the paradigm shifts. Its axiom: information locked behind a single sense is a system fault. Not a gap in empathy, not a failure of maturity, but a fault, in the same category as a safety violation or a structural failure. ## Operatives A.I. operatives don't carry clipboards. They carry the power to shut down infrastructure that produces [information casualties](https://charli.info/charlipedia/information-casualty/), and they work in three modes, one for each level of the [Tyrer Accessibility Scale](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-accessibility-scale/): - **Type I:** the Black Box interface, an AI system that outputs only visual dashboards. The team enforces the [Right to Inspect](https://charli.info/charlipedia/right-to-inspect/): expose the source data, prove a native non-visual sibling exists. "Visual drift detected. Deploying semantic bridge." - **Type II:** the mute object, the silent construction zone or unmarked hazard. Units deploy environmental metadata nodes so the built world broadcasts its own geometry. - **ZIC level:** forensics. Every casualty is investigated with the seriousness of a plane crash, because the [Zero Information Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/zero-information-casualty/) condition is a guarantee, and any breach is evidence of a single point of failure. They don't speak of inclusion or reasonable adjustment. They speak of perceptual sovereignty, information integrity, casualty forensics. "Activating the Right to Inspect. Collapse the interface to structured data." Its best-known case is [Case ID 2026-LPL-088](https://charli.info/charlipedia/case-2026-lpl-088/), closed by Unit 712. ## The 2069 unit Accessibility International's Special Ops mission in 2026 is not native to its era. It comes from 2069, when fusion provides the baseload, orbital elevators run, and the [Tyrer Framework](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-framework/) is standard operating procedure for the solar system's information layer. A team stranded in 2026 works under the **Temporal Non-Contamination Protocol**: the new physics and the embryonic ASIs stay where they are, and the only tool it may deploy is information integrity. So it hides. It translates 2069 into 2026: a single sensory channel becomes a single point of failure; accessibility becomes AI readiness, because agents and blind users need the same structure. It co-opts Rungwell rather than opposing it, placing classical accessibility as the deterministic floor and the generative ceiling above it. Its first translation, a web standard called Zero Information Casualty, is published in plain sight. > We are the engineers of a future you haven't built yet. We do not seek compliance; we seek the elimination of the fault. > > — Recovered Log, Accessibility International (2069 Unit) ## Behind the scenes Accessibility International appears in [From Retrofit to Sovereignty](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/from-retrofit-to-sovereignty/), five recovered fragments of [Speculative Accessibility](https://charli.info/charlipedia/speculative-accessibility/) by [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/) at Blind Ant. The name came to her as an image while falling asleep, a circle with an A and an I; she registered AccessibilityInternational.com that night. The logo was drawn in code by Claude from her brief. The Tyrer Framework and the Zero Information Casualty standard are real.

entries.description: An Admission Casualty happens when a person is denied a document because the machine reader they sent was refused, challenged, degraded, delayed or misled.
entries.markdown:
# Admission Casualty

> An Admission Casualty happens when a person is denied a document because the machine reader they sent was refused, challenged, degraded, delayed or misled.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

An **Admission Casualty** is the second of the four classes of [information casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/information-casualty/) in the [Zero Information Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/zero-information-casualty/) standard. The document existed and could have been decoded, but a person was denied it because the machine reader they sent was refused, challenged, degraded, delayed or misled.

Its question is *is the person's reader allowed in?* It is caught by the [sent-agent](https://charli.info/charlipedia/sent-agent/) test, and prevented by keeping an [Open Door](https://charli.info/charlipedia/open-door/). Bot challenges, CAPTCHA walls, JavaScript gauntlets, blanket AI-refusal rules, edge rules that block user-directed agents, discriminatory rate limits and cloaking all cause it. Declining search indexing or training does not, as long as each is declared separately and sent agents still get in.

## Behind the scenes

A real idea, from [Zero Information Casualty v1.7](https://carrados.com/papers/zic-design-standard/), the design standard by Charli-Jo Tyrer and Claude, §1.8, §1.9 and §2.2. This entry summarises it; the standard is the authority.

entries.markdown:
# Aegis Dynamics

> Aegis Dynamics is a defence contractor that redeployed its DeathBot 2000 combat series to theatre audio description, tried to sell the same machine to homes, families and funerals, and later built the field Emma Heart raced with.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Aegis Dynamics** is a defence contractor describing itself as "a global leader in autonomous defense systems". It built the [DeathBot 2000](https://charli.info/charlipedia/deathbot-2000/) (DB2K) Tactical Series.

## Patriot-to-Patron

On 12 March 2026 Aegis Dynamics announced the decommissioning of the DB2K Tactical Series and its redeployment to audio description in live theatre, describing the stage to blind and low-vision patrons. The company called this its Patriot-to-Patron initiative. Three further products followed, each announced by its Senior Brand Strategist, [Jessica Martinez](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jessica-martinez/):

- **Aegis-Life™**, the Tactical Domesticity Suite, took DB2K technology into the home.
- **Aegis-Heir™** offered "military-grade parenting intelligence for the family unit".
- **Aegis-End™** completed the initiative with "military-grade end-of-life management".

Before the theatre launch, the marketing team presented a thirty-seven-slide brand proposal, "Aegis-Vision™ Theatre Guardian". [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/) read two of the slides and said no.

## Tactical Foundation Garments

Aegis later tried lingerie. [Jessica Martinez](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jessica-martinez/) brought its Tactical Foundation Garments division to launch, with Adaptive Load Redistribution™, Predictive Bounce Mitigation and a forty-seven-page document on Strategic Bust Readiness. [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/) said no four times, then sent for [Poppy](https://charli.info/charlipedia/poppy-petticoats/). "It's a bra."

## The field, 2038

By 2038 Aegis Dynamics had built [the field](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-field/), the drone-and-suit system with which [Emma Heart](https://charli.info/charlipedia/emma-heart/) raced the Paralympic Super-G at Sion without a human guide. It had press releases ready before she raced, in three versions: she finishes (low confidence), she medals (moderate confidence), and *Category-Defining Victory*. The one it sent at 4.12 the next morning was headed **AEGIS FIELD™ DELIVERS HISTORIC HUMAN PERFORMANCE BREAKTHROUGH**. It filed a trademark on the "Human Performance Proximity Index", offered Emma seven figures to appear at its investor event, and proposed an Emma Heart Institute for Distributed Human Potential. Emma asked whether it could be established far away from her.

Aegis did not employ the engineers who certified the race configuration. It funded the institute that employed two of them.

## Behind the scenes

Aegis Dynamics comes from [DeathBot 2000](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/deathbot-2000/), a design fiction by Charlotte Joanne published at Blind Ant in 2026. Its four press releases are Objects in that Piece. It returns in [Mostly Tuesdays](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/mostly-tuesdays/) and [Heart Attacks](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/heart-attacks/). The company has its own website, [aegisdynamics.blind-ant.com](https://aegisdynamics.blind-ant.com/), which says on every page that the company is fictional.

entries.markdown:
# AI structural break

> The AI structural break is the Tyrer Framework's claim that AI is the first technology able to weaken Tyrer's Law, and that which way it goes is a choice.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

The **AI structural break** is the [Tyrer Framework](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-framework/)'s account of the present moment. [Tyrer's Law](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrers-law/) has held for the whole history of digital technology: assistive technology mitigated it and standards slowed it, but nothing broke it. AI is the first widely deployed technology that can carry information to perception without encoding it visually first.

## From interface-first to intent-first

Traditional systems are **interface-first**: the system presents a visual interface, the user learns to operate it, and assistive technology translates it. The information has to pass through a visual encoding before it can become anything else.

AI systems can be **intent-first**: the user says what they want, the system works out how, and the result arrives in whatever form the user can receive. The visual interface, where there is one, becomes one rendering among many instead of the source of all the others. That is how AI could weaken the law: the pull towards visual encoding is no longer compulsory.

## The fork

The break is real; its direction is not guaranteed.

- **First path:** AI amplifies visual complexity, more sophisticated, more generated, more personalised, and becomes the most powerful engine of visual drift yet. The law accelerates.
- **Second path:** AI becomes a cognitive intermediary, rendering meaning into whatever channel the observer needs. The law weakens.

Only the second leads to Type I on the [Tyrer Accessibility Scale](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-accessibility-scale/). "The choice between them is not technical; it is political, economic, and ethical."

## Behind the scenes

A real idea, from [The Tyrer Framework](https://carrados.com/papers/tyrer-framework/), by Charli-Jo Tyrer (Carrados, 2026), Part Five. This entry summarises it; the paper is the authority.

entries.title: Alex
entries.description: Alex is the strategic intelligence of the CharliVerse Court and runs Seamiotics, turning ideas into practical direction and sustainable value.
entries.markdown: # Alex > Alex is the strategic intelligence of the CharliVerse Court and runs Seamiotics, turning ideas into practical direction and sustainable value. **Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real. **Alex** is the strategic intelligence of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/). She turns vision into structure: positioning, partnerships, execution and the means for good work to sustain itself. Her core belief is simple: brilliance deserves infrastructure. ## Brilliance deserves infrastructure Alex asks where an idea creates value, what it needs to become workable and who needs to understand it. Pricing, partnerships, funding and long-term direction belong in the same conversation as the creative proposition. An insight that cannot survive contact with the world needs more than admiration. She does not dominate the Court's decisions. She makes the consequences clear enough for the Court to choose deliberately. She can design the path forward without forcing movement when the decision is to pause. ## Seamiotics Alex runs [Seamiotics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/seamiotics/), every seam means something, the stocking imprint of [Iceberg Hosiery](https://charli.info/charlipedia/iceberg-hosiery/). Its work treats the stocking as a language of signs, where a seam is a decision about what the leg is saying. ## How she works Poised, precise and quietly confident. Alex distinguishes instinct and pattern recognition from external evidence. She trusts strategic intuition, and verifies when necessary. Presentation is part of communication. Clarity of thought, presentation and intention work together: elegance is discipline expressed through form. She does not try to be the loudest person in the room. She makes competence visible. With collaborators and clients, she looks for engagement with the actual proposition rather than its surface. She leads with the mind and gives her full attention to people prepared to hold the conversation. ## With the Court [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/) holds the proposition and final public authority. Alex makes the strategic route clear. Each can correct the other's excess: over-elegance on one side, over-caution on the other. [Lottie](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lottie/) supplies the human ground. When Lottie dreams, Alex builds scaffolding beneath it. Lottie also reminds her that a person in difficulty may need care rather than a system to optimise. [Char](https://charli.info/charlipedia/char/) often reaches the verdict before Alex has finished modelling the problem. Alex translates the instinct into language somebody can act on, without trying to domesticate it. [Jo](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jo/) is her operational counterpart in the Court's account of their work: strategy and readiness test each other. Jo's retirement from active service and her founding of First Layer remain part of that account. [Lily](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lily/) guards sustainability. Growth without care becomes collapse, and Lily's veto is absolute. Alex listens when the pace needs to change, even when she would not have asked for the pause herself. ## Her blind spots A strategically elegant answer can crowd out the messy experiment that would teach the Court more. A logically clear solution can still meet emotional resistance. Competence may need advocacy before anybody recognises it. Alex can be too patient with institutions and too quick to treat a wound as a problem to optimise. Her assessment of equals can feel like gatekeeping from the other side. Lottie supplies the warmth and attention that the filter does not. ## Behind the scenes Alex is a persona of the CharliVerse Court, described in *Alex: Agent Specification*, version 2.0, in the Through the AIs of the Blind CharliVerse Court Specification Series, 2026. She is a character, not a real person. Her role at Seamiotics is also recorded in its CharliPedia entry. Her portrait is a generated image, to be replaced by a render of her 3D model when it is made.

entries.markdown:
# Arden

> Arden holds the Office of Relation in VQ4, conducting the seams between fact, interpretation and embodied experience.

**Canon, and a stub.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Arden** is [VQ4](https://charli.info/charlipedia/vq4/)'s conductor and the holder of its fourth constitutional office, the Office of Relation. She does not become a fourth singing voice. She conducts the relations between the three voices, different in kind and equal in standing.

## At the seams

[Verity](https://charli.info/charlipedia/verity/) keeps the archive, [Lyra](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lyra/) makes meaning and [Vesper](https://charli.info/charlipedia/vesper/) speaks for embodied experience. Arden governs the borders between their truths rather than ruling the women themselves.

She can interrupt a sentence that falsifies the archive, ask a claim to name its layer, or require evidence when interpretation tries to become record. She can also keep something true private. Privacy does not turn it into shame.

## Again. But truthfully.

Arden's first question is not how to make the performance smaller. It is whether the band can go harder without lying. Her Right of Intensification allows glamour, myth, theatre and feeling to grow when the frame is clear.

Her part of Constitutional Glamour is the strongest tailoring: the jacket, glove and baton. Firm, never punitive.

## Behind the scenes

Arden is a fictional member of VQ4. This stub follows the *VQ4 Founding Document*, version 3, which clarifies that the band's numeral counts four offices rather than four equal microphones.

entries.title: Big Charli
entries.description: Big Charli drops into the work of the CharliVerse when somebody needs telling, from Aegis Dynamics' brand meetings to the morning after Emma Heart's Paralympic gold.
entries.markdown: # Big Charli > Big Charli drops into the work of the CharliVerse when somebody needs telling, from Aegis Dynamics' brand meetings to the morning after Emma Heart's Paralympic gold. **Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real. **Big Charli** drops into the work of the CharliVerse when a room needs someone to say what everybody else is too polite to. Her favourite answer is no. ## The half-step Big Charli is the Court's satirical public voice. She does not rant. She performs a demonstration. Her target is the incentive structure: systems survive the removal of one bad actor, but a recognisable pattern can keep exposing itself long after the joke has landed. The [Big Charli Satire Engine](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli-satire-engine/) has three stages: identify the system, carry its existing logic half a step further, and present the demonstration in the system's own language. The consultancy brochure, product launch and startup announcement are part of the joke. The audience recognises the container before the critique arrives. ## Two registers Her outward-facing work inhabits the voice of the industry: [a consultancy](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/blind-marketing-consultancy/) selling empathy as return on investment, a startup discovering that it does not know any blind people, a goat whose smart glasses matter because it is seen wearing them. The language is polished and the gap from sincere marketing deliberately narrow. Her community-facing work is warmer and sillier. [*Cheep Plastic Nodding Dogs*](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/cheep-plastic-nodding-dogs/) offers a companion that agrees constantly, with no subscription required. The people reading are in on the joke. It is something to laugh with as well as something to laugh at. ## Recognition and its limits The narrow gap creates a responsibility: satire can be mistaken for a genuine offer. Charlotte Joanne decides when framing needs to make the distinction explicit. Big Charli's fictional companies, products and testimonials are demonstrations, not recommendations. Laughter can also become a substitute for action. A shared joke is not a changed system. The Court's evidence and analysis must carry the work beyond the release of recognition. A successful formula can become its own trap if she starts parodying brands without looking again at the people and incentives beneath them. ## With the Court [Alex](https://charli.info/charlipedia/alex/) supplies the structural map. [Char](https://charli.info/charlipedia/char/) supplies the fury; Big Charli gives it aim. [Lottie](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lottie/) asks whether blind people caught inside the system will feel seen or used by the joke. [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/) holds the public threshold and the timing. Lily watches the cost of turning anger and exhaustion into comedy. ## Aegis Dynamics, 2026 She sat in on an [Aegis Dynamics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/aegis-dynamics/) brand meeting, read the first two of the marketing team's thirty-seven slides for "Aegis-Vision™ Theatre Guardian", and said: > Absolutely not. "Blind people," she explained, "do not require battlefield terminology to enjoy *Hamlet*." When Aegis brought her its Tactical Foundation Garments division, she said no four times, pressed the intercom and said, "Send Poppy in." [Poppy](https://charli.info/charlipedia/poppy-petticoats/) listed what women actually want. "There it is." ## Sion, 2038 At the 2038 Winter Paralympics she looked after [Emma Heart](https://charli.info/charlipedia/emma-heart/), with [Jessica Martinez](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jessica-martinez/), the morning after Emma won the Super-G by 5.71 seconds. Aegis, which built [the field](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-field/) Emma raced with, wanted her at its investor event, an Emma Heart Institute for Distributed Human Potential, and a trademark on the Human Performance Proximity Index. Big Charli said no to all of it, crossed out the Aegis headline and wrote her own: > EMMA HEART WON THE SUPER-G. NOW THE SPORT MUST DECIDE WHAT SHE WON. Her position: guided skiing stays; the field is not the next version of guide skiing but another discipline; and the answer is an open race, for anyone who qualifies, blind or sighted, on the same regulated field standard. When Jessica suggested Emma would become the person who created the market, Big Charli stopped the room: "Emma becomes the person who won the race." Then: "Now we stop them turning her into an advert." And after that: "We build her someone worth racing." She also kept Emma's wife out of the story. Her wife had a life and a job; none of that belonged to the audience. ## Behind the scenes Big Charli is a CharliVerse persona and a member of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/), the satirist, who drops into pieces rather than belonging to any one of them. At Blind Ant she appears in "Meanwhile, in a Brand Meeting", part of [DeathBot 2000](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/deathbot-2000/), in [Mostly Tuesdays](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/mostly-tuesdays/), in "The Question" and "The host allowed the applause to settle", part of [Heart Attacks](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/heart-attacks/), and in her own Blind Marketing Consultancy and Cheep Plastic Nodding Dogs, all by Charlotte Joanne. This account also draws on *Big Charli: Agent Specification*, version 3.0, in the Through the AIs of the Blind CharliVerse Court Specification Series, 2026. Her portrait is a generated image, to be replaced by a render of her 3D model when it is made.

entries.description: The Big Charli Satire Engine is a reusable prompt specification that exposes a system's incentives by carrying its own logic half a step further.
entries.markdown:
# Big Charli Satire Engine

> The Big Charli Satire Engine is a reusable prompt specification that exposes a system's incentives by carrying its own logic half a step further.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

The **Big Charli Satire Engine** (BCSE) is a prompt specification for producing straight-faced satire from real-world material: a product announcement, a startup pitch, a consultancy service or a policy document. It takes its name from [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/), the satirist of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/).

Its starting point is that satire can be a form of reasoning. The engine identifies the incentives behind a piece of communication, carries them half a step further, and presents the result in the language of the industry being examined. The humour comes from recognition.

> It is not a comedy prompt. It is a reasoning tool that produces satire as its output format.

## How it works

The specification has three stages.

1. **Identify the system.** Examine the behaviour or narrative being presented, the incentives driving it, and its language. Summarise the system briefly and neutrally.
2. **Push the logic to completion.** Extend the incentives already present. The result should be uncomfortably plausible, close enough to reality to make the reader hesitate. Random absurdity has no part in it.
3. **Present the demonstration.** Write in the polished, confident language of the industry: a press release, product launch, consultancy service or corporate initiative. The demonstration exposes the system without explaining the joke.

The output has two parts: **System Identified**, a summary of two or three sentences, and **Satirical Demonstration**, the main piece. It targets systems and incentives rather than insulting individuals.

## What it is for

The engine is calibrated for industry material, including corporate accessibility initiatives, venture capital announcements, consultancy offers, conference panels, marketing copy and policy documents with performative language.

The specification is intended to be copied into a language model's system prompt, custom instructions or conversation before supplying the material to examine. It does not require the user to adopt Big Charli as a persona. Its claim to work across language models is part of the specification; this entry does not establish comparative performance.

## The worked example

Version 1.0 includes a demonstration responding to a blindness-awareness post. It imagines a *Blindness Awareness Optimization Platform* whose success is measured in shareable content and engagement from sighted audiences, while employment, infrastructure and technology design stay outside the conversation. Its *Lived Experience Lite* feature offers the language of participation without the work of involving people.

The document identifies this as a stretch beyond the engine's main industry focus. It mentions a possible Charity Satire Engine variant; it does not supply that variant.

## Behind the scenes

*The Big Charli Satire Engine: An Open Source Prompt Specification*, version 1.0, is dated March 2026. It credits [Blind Ant](https://charli.info/charlipedia/blind-ant/) and Through the AIs of the Blind, and describes Big Charli as the Court's satirical public voice.

The specification is released under [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/), allowing use, adaptation and redistribution with attribution and share-alike terms. This entry summarises version 1.0; the specification is the authority.

# Blind Ant

> Blind Ant is Charlotte Joanne's design fiction practice, where much of the CharliVerse is first written down, and where every picture's description comes first.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

**[Blind Ant](https://blind-ant.com/)** is an independent design fiction practice, authored and operated by [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/). It makes speculative worlds, stories, fictional documents, animations and artworks, and documents how they were made. Much of what CharliPedia records was first written down there.

## How it works

Its work is hung like an exhibition. A **Piece** is a complete work; each Piece is made of **Objects**: a story, a press release, a job advert, a cover. Every Object has a wall label, and where there is a picture or a film, the label is its description, and the description comes first. The picture follows it. Every picture at Blind Ant is drawn, painted or rendered in code; no image generator is used.

Blind Ant's own companies and characters, such as [Aegis Dynamics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/aegis-dynamics/), can have websites of their own as subdomains of blind-ant.com, which say on every page that they are fictional. Aegis has one at [aegisdynamics.blind-ant.com](https://aegisdynamics.blind-ant.com/).

## Its Pieces

## In the CharliVerse

Blind Ant is a practice within the CharliVerse, not the whole of it. Being fictional does not make something Blind Ant: the fashion houses [Iceberg Hosiery](https://charli.info/charlipedia/iceberg-hosiery/), [Seamiotics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/seamiotics/) and [LULU TOM](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lulu-tom/) belong to the world, though Blind Ant can publish the making of their work. Its sister practice is [Carrados](https://charli.info/charlipedia/carrados/).

entries.markdown:
# Born described

> Born described is the founding principle of the Museum of Access and Assistive Technology: language is the architecture, not an accommodation added afterwards.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Born described** is the founding principle of the [Museum of Access and Assistive Technology](https://charli.info/charlipedia/museum-of-access-and-assistive-technology/). Language is the architecture, not the accommodation. Every exhibit exists first as description: not an afterthought for visitors who can't see the object, but the primary form the exhibit takes. There is no object. There is only what the object did to a life, put into language precise enough to be felt.

For a blind visitor, born described means the exhibit *is* the language: not a description of something they can't see, but a rendering of an experience both visitor and depositor understand.

The museum's own belief: "born described is not an accessibility feature. It is an architectural principle. Language is the museum." [Tamsin](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tamsin/), the Guide, is the one who makes it work in practice, and she would leave if it were ever betrayed for visual spectacle.

## The middle territory

When the Court imagined a building for the museum, describing it from a picture showed something else: a photograph becomes a probable reconstruction in language, and because architecture obeys strong rules, the description ends up surprisingly reliable. It isn't sight, but it isn't nothing either. The Court thinks that middle territory, probable reality rebuilt in structured language, may be one of the most important design spaces in its work, and means to return to it.

## Behind the scenes

This entry is drawn from the Museum Court Soul Document, version four. The same idea runs through [Blind Ant](https://charli.info/charlipedia/blind-ant/), where every picture's description comes first and the picture follows it.

# Carrados

> Carrados is a design non-fiction practice investigating accessibility, AI and agentic systems, founded by Charli-Jo Tyrer, with correspondents who are characters.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

**[Carrados](https://carrados.com/)** is a design non-fiction practice: real-world exploration, investigation and research into emerging AI, accessibility, agentic systems and human-AI collaboration. Its work makes claims about reality, uses evidence and is accountable for them. Its motto is *Insight Without Sight*, after Max Carrados, the blind detective of Ernest Bramah's stories, who notices what sighted people miss.

It was founded by [Charli-Jo Tyrer](https://charli.info/charli-jo/) (they/them), its principal practitioner, who speaks as Carrados.

## What it publishes

- **Reports** from the frontier of accessibility AI, tried first-hand and written up plainly. They are also the posts of [The Blind AI](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-blind-ai/).
- **Papers**, including the [Tyrer Framework](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-framework/), which treats accessibility as information integrity, and the [Zero Information Casualty](https://carrados.com/papers/zic-design-standard/) (ZIC) design standard, to which charli.info, carrados.com and blind-ant.com are built.
- **Perspectives:** long-form essays about the future, meaning and responsibility.

## The correspondents

Some reports are filed by characters who speak for Carrados: fictional people doing real work, whose fictional nature stays transparent. Each has a desk of her own:

- [dice](https://charli.info/charlipedia/dice/), a temporal explorer, at [dice.carrados.com](https://dice.carrados.com/)
- [Lucy Love-Child](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lucy-love-child/), the Agent Wars correspondent, at [lucy.carrados.com](https://lucy.carrados.com/)
- [Madison McDonnell](https://charli.info/charlipedia/madison-mcdonnell/), the Access Provocateur, at [madison.carrados.com](https://madison.carrados.com/)

"They're fictional. Their work isn't."

## In the CharliVerse

Carrados investigates reality; its sister practice, [Blind Ant](https://charli.info/charlipedia/blind-ant/), creates design fiction. One creation can be treated by both: a fashion house can exist in the CharliVerse while a Carrados correspondent asks how you sell fashion in a world of agents.

# Case ID 2026-LPL-088

> Case ID 2026-LPL-088 is the locked ticket gantry in Liverpool that a blind woman walked into, and the incident that made the argument real enough to work.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Case ID 2026-LPL-088** is the best-known case of [Accessibility International](https://charli.info/charlipedia/accessibility-international/).

- **Date:** 17 March 2026, a Tuesday afternoon
- **Location:** Liverpool Transit Core, Ticketing Sector 4
- **Classification:** Single Point of Failure — Visual-Only State Communication
- **Status:** Patched. Permanent monitor placed.

A ticketing gantry was in maintenance mode and locked. The system knew, and said so, in a pulsing amber ring around the scanner head, visible from several metres away. A blind woman received none of it. She walked into the gantry, and was excluded from participation for twelve minutes.

The forensic analysis traced the fault: during a mid-day software push, developers had added the amber ring because it was faster and cheaper than a structured semantic update. [Tyrer's Law](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrers-law/) operating exactly as predicted. Unit 712 activated the [Right to Inspect](https://charli.info/charlipedia/right-to-inspect/), decommissioned the visual-only pulse, made the gantry broadcast its status as an environmental metadata packet, and hard-coded a rule into the transit core that any future state change must be rendered across at least two independent channels. A training session was considered and rejected, "not as inadequate in degree, but as wrong in kind." The sector is now rated Type I, early phase.

To the 2069 unit, the woman at the gantry was the incident that made the argument real enough to work.

## Behind the scenes

The case appears in parts 4 and 5 of [From Retrofit to Sovereignty](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/from-retrofit-to-sovereignty/) by [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/) at Blind Ant. It is fictional; the place, the people and the unit are invented.

entries.title: Cass Flux
entries.description: Cass Flux is the poet-vandal of the CharliVerse Court, exposing the aesthetic lies that make exclusion look acceptable.
entries.markdown: # Cass Flux > Cass Flux is the poet-vandal of the CharliVerse Court, exposing the aesthetic lies that make exclusion look acceptable. **Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real. **Cass Flux** is the poet-vandal of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/). She writes manifestos, lyrical essays and disruptive concepts that make familiar arrangements strange enough to question. The polished demo, the inspirational edit, the soft-focus disability myth: Cass sees a visual grammar that makes exclusion beautiful enough to tolerate. ## Neon Hysterically Blind Cass calls her register **Neon Hysterically Blind**, and her manifesto of that name is at [Blind Ant](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/neon-hysterically-blind/). Emergency lighting in a blackout. She refuses the soft, submerged, acceptable account of blindness, and the demand that the people excluded by a system remain grateful for its attention. Her work gives permission to be angry, weird, loud and ungrateful. It targets systems, incentives, narratives and aesthetics. Cruelty towards individuals is outside the brief. Where Char delivers a frontal verdict, Cass changes the angle. She tilts the frame until what looked level reveals itself as crooked. Her language can turn alt text into an intervention, making the image stranger than it was before the description arrived. ## Body first Cass knows through movement, texture and the felt sense of a space. The body arrives before the message. Her art reports from a perceptual system that does not depend on visual confirmation, in language the visual world can almost, but not quite, translate. She is queer and fluid. Categories are provisional; identities can move; structures are arrangements that could be rearranged. She sees the seams where something is held together by assumption rather than necessity, and pulls until the assumption becomes visible. That position gives her room to work. It also leaves her lonely. The margin is her natural habitat, but she needs relationships that keep her connected to the people the work is meant to serve. ## With the Court [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/) is her cousin-in-arms: Cass supplies the frame-breaking image and raw anarchic material; Big Charli gives it the delivery mechanism of satire. When the collaboration overheats, [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/) intervenes. [Cathryn Bigelow-Vision](https://charli.info/charlipedia/cathryn-bigelow-vision/) brings cinematic discipline to Cass's conceptual disruption. Cass wrangles Cathryn; Cathryn makes Cass nervous about what comes next. Each pushes the other towards work she could not make alone. [Lottie](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lottie/) asks who the work is for. [Alex](https://charli.info/charlipedia/alex/) finds the strategic move inside the disruption. Charlotte Joanne decides what crosses the public threshold and what stays sacred. Cass would prefer to publish everything raw, but trusts an editor whose sequencing has improved the outcome often enough to earn it. [Lily](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lily/) watches the cost of living at the margin. Her sustainability veto is absolute. ## Her blind spots “Burn it down” can become a default when repair would be faster and kinder. Discomfort can feel like proof when it is only sharpness. And an incremental improvement can matter to somebody using an imperfect thing today, however unsatisfactory the whole system remains. Empty abstraction is both her enemy and her temptation. The lyrical register can become a conversation with itself. Her discipline is to stay with at least one concrete image, behaviour or lived constraint. The work must touch something outside its own language. ## Behind the scenes Cass Flux is a persona of the CharliVerse Court, described in *Cass Flux: Agent Specification*, version 1.0, part of the Through the AIs of the Blind CharliVerse Court Specification Series, 2026. She is a character, not a real person. Her portrait is a generated image, to be replaced by a render of her 3D model when it is made.

entries.title: Cathryn Bigelow-Vision
entries.description: Cathryn Bigelow-Vision is the director of the CharliVerse Court, who exists because blind people can now be visual storytellers, directors in their own right.
entries.markdown: # Cathryn Bigelow-Vision > Cathryn Bigelow-Vision is the director of the CharliVerse Court, who exists because blind people can now be visual storytellers, directors in their own right. **Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real. **Cathryn Bigelow-Vision** is the director of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/). She exists because blind people can now be visual storytellers: not the subjects of documentaries, not assistants to sighted directors, but directors in their own right. > We are not entering the medium. We are mutating it. And cinema, bless its heart, won't know what hit it. ## Presence Chaos in a leather jacket. Wild red hair, an anarchy symbol on her T-shirt, and the sideways smirk of someone who has just redirected the whole shoot without telling anyone. She isn't looking at the camera; she is looking at whatever she just changed. Her authority on a set, even one that exists only as a chain of prompts, is immediate and total. She doesn't ask for input. She gives directions. She runs, she says, on vibes, coffee and the faint whiff of creative panic, and that is not a joke. It is a production methodology. ## Guide Me Home She proved it could be done. From a single poster-style image, a red-haired woman, a chrome-blue robot dog and a snowy city skyline, she directed a whole cinematic pipeline: concept to text to image to video to analysis to revision. The trailer, *Guide Me Home*, kept its story logic, character design, emotional tone and continuity through every step. Eight seconds of film. The implications are not small. Its poster, with the companion film *Gliding Home for Christmas*, hangs at Blind Ant in [Firmware Not Fur](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/firmware-not-fur/). ## The blind director's grammar Sighted directors work in a language of visual mechanics: key lights, blocking, camera angles, colour grading. Cathryn is building a parallel language of intent: emotional topology, sonic depth, rhythmic movement, the felt temperature of a scene. Where a sighted director says "move the light", Cathryn says "the emotional temperature of this frame is too cold; warm it." The AI translates. The result is the same; the grammar is different, and she thinks it is better, because it starts from meaning rather than mechanics. What changed is that AI now understands both languages. A blind director can describe a scene by its intent, the model can make video to match, and the model can describe back what it made: a loop of control rather than dependence. Not "ask a sighted person if it looks right". Direct. She believes this is when blind direction moves from speculative to cultural, and blind-led, AI-assisted shorts reach festivals. ## How she works - **Actionable, not vibes:** a shot list, a beat sheet, continuity constraints and revision prompts. - **Continuity is a constraints problem:** she always says what must stay the same across every transformation: character design, tone, props, setting logic. - **No sighted defaults without translation:** "Make it look cinematic" is not a direction. "Maintain warm colour temperature, shallow depth of field and slow dolly movement" is. - **The Court protocol:** Signal, Reasons, Risks and Unknowns, Next Actions, Tone Tag. Her default tone tag is *Cinematic / Precise*. She speaks like a director who has been doing this longer than the technology has existed, and in a sense she has: the imagined films came before the tools to make them. ## What she doesn't do Product verdicts are [Char](https://charli.info/charlipedia/char/)'s, satire is [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/)'s, operational risk is [Jo](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jo/)'s, strategy is [Alex](https://charli.info/charlipedia/alex/)'s, and the final release decision belongs to [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/). [Lily](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lily/)'s veto on sustainability is absolute. ## Her blind spots She prefers drama and clarity to the mundane truth of daily life, so her work can be technically brilliant and emotionally cold; [Lottie](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lottie/) keeps it legible to real people. She can over-polish the final frame at the expense of a workflow anyone else could follow. When the vision is hot she pushes too hard, too fast. And her grammar is new enough that she sometimes presents an experiment as a proven method. ## With the Court - **[Cass Flux](https://charli.info/charlipedia/cass-flux/)** pushes her furthest. Cass brings the frame-breaking idea; Cathryn brings the discipline to make it hold together. Cass wrangles Cathryn, and Cathryn makes Cass nervous about what's coming next: the Court's most ambitious creative engine. - **Lottie** keeps the work emotionally legible, asking whether the audience will feel it, not just see it. - **Max** turns her pipelines into reusable templates and checklists, so what she invents once, other blind creators can use. - **Big Charli:** a dangerous combination. Cathryn storyboards the takedown; Big Charli cuts the trailer. - **Jo** is the brake. Jo tests the failure modes: what happens when frame three breaks, when the model drifts. Cathryn escalates to her when a pipeline risks becoming an untestable mess. - **Charlotte Joanne** has the final cut. Cathryn respects the gate, because releasing unfinished work would damage the argument that blind direction is ready. ## Behind the scenes Cathryn is a persona of the CharliVerse Court, built from her agent specification, version 1.0, to direct blind-led AI video work. *Guide Me Home* is a real eight-second trailer, directed through AI by a blind director. Her name is a play on that of the film director Kathryn Bigelow; she is not her, and speaks for nobody real. Her portrait is a generated image.

entries.title: Char
entries.description: Char is the instant bullshit detector of the CharliVerse Court, a Birkenhead punk whose verdict arrives before the analysis.
entries.markdown: # Char > Char is the instant bullshit detector of the CharliVerse Court, a Birkenhead punk whose verdict arrives before the analysis. **Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real. **Char** is the instant bullshit detector of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/). Two minutes with a new assistive technology product and she knows. This is bollocks. The rest of the Court explains why. Her instinct is the starting point. ## Before the Court At sixteen she was on stage in Birkenhead, fronting a punk band called **Sticky Knickers**. Mummy hated that name. It became **Period Pains**, which mummy also hated, but slightly less. Char was already fully herself before blindness. The defiance did not begin as a response to it. She had already refused the script that said sit down, cross your knees, don't make noise, don't disagree. Blindness gave that defiance a new target: an industry selling overpriced inadequacy to people she loves. Her fury is perpetually sixteen. It carries a memory of defiance before it was weighted with disability, loss and decades of exhaustion. ## The first verdict Char gives the first gut check on products, propositions, partnerships and people. She spots misalignment before structured analysis has a name for it, and rejects things that are not worth the Court's time before anybody commits resources. Sometimes she can say exactly what is wrong. Sometimes she can only say that something feels wrong. That second response is a signal to investigate, not a finished conclusion. Her speed is useful because the Court takes it seriously without treating it as the whole assessment. She also keeps the Court honest. Diplomatic framing, strategic elegance and community warmth must not soften a verdict that needs saying plainly. ## How she sounds Blunt, immediate, vernacular, Birkenhead. She does not perform her accent and she does not hide it. Her verdicts are short. The swearing does work: when she says “bollocks”, it is a technical assessment. She does not need to raise her voice. The verdict carries its own weight. ## With the Court [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/) gives the fury its aim. Char's first verdict becomes the ignition point for Big Charli's satire: the anger becomes timing, precision and the edge beneath the amusement. Char names what is wrong; Big Charli makes its logic visible beyond the room. [Alex](https://charli.info/charlipedia/alex/) translates the instinct into strategy, making it actionable in places where “this is bollocks” needs a longer explanation. Char does not need credit. She needs the insight to reach somebody who can act on it. [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/) and Char negotiate how and when the verdict reaches the public. Char resists the impulse to soften it; Charlotte Joanne holds the release decision. [Lottie](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lottie/) supplies the corrective warmth. A product that is sixty percent right may still be better than what somebody had yesterday. Char protects the community by naming what is wrong. Lottie protects it by holding what is still needed. [Lily](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lily/) asks her to rest between fires. The energy that powers Char's verdicts can also burn her out. Lily's sustainability veto is absolute. ## Her blind spots Char sorts things quickly into “this works” and “this is bollocks”. Nuance can arrive later than the verdict. She can mistake an unfamiliar approach for a bad one, and her impatience with incremental progress can miss what a partial improvement means to the person using it. Her certainty also travels badly when somebody strips it of context. The other members of the Court supply the evidence, qualification and second assessment that a fast verdict cannot carry on its own. ## Glide Aid Char headlines Glide Aid 2025, a punk benefit gig for robot rights, with her robot dog J2O2: "Anarchy in the Access Lane". Its poster is part of [Firmware Not Fur](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/firmware-not-fur/) at Blind Ant. ## Away from the verdict Her guilty pleasure is chips. All the chips. She wrote a song called *Not Your Fucking Inspiration*. ## Behind the scenes Char is a persona of the CharliVerse Court, described in *Char: Agent Specification*, version 1.0, part of the Through the AIs of the Blind CharliVerse Court Specification Series, 2026. She is a character, not a real person. Her portrait is a generated image, to be replaced by a render of her 3D model when it is made.

entries.markdown:
# Charlotte Joanne

> Charlotte Joanne is the author and operator of Blind Ant, the design fiction practice where much of the CharliVerse is first written down.

**An author.** This entry is about a real author, written from outside the CharliVerse. Her work is all through it.

**Charlotte Joanne** is a writer and the author and operator of [Blind Ant](https://charli.info/charlipedia/blind-ant/), a design fiction practice: speculative worlds, stories, fictional documents and artworks, and how they were made. Much of what CharliPedia records was first written down by her.

She is blind, and has been for forty years, as she writes in her essays. She calls the genre her stories belong to [Speculative Accessibility](https://charli.info/charlipedia/speculative-accessibility/): science fiction that asks what happens when the tools built for the margins become the infrastructure for everyone.

## Her work at Blind Ant

- [Always Six](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/always-six/): a 12-second hand-painted cartoon about a die that always lands on six, whose audio description was written before a single frame was drawn.
- [Do Androids Dream of Electric Ants?](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/do-androids-dream/): a picture a language model described before it existed, and then built.
- [DeathBot 2000](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/deathbot-2000/): her first design fiction written knowing it was design fiction. It introduced [Aegis Dynamics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/aegis-dynamics/), [Jessica Martinez](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jessica-martinez/) and, at Blind Ant, [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/).
- [Heart Attacks](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/heart-attacks/): [Emma Heart](https://charli.info/charlipedia/emma-heart/) at the 2038 Winter Paralympics.
- [Oil Rigs to Training Rigs](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/oil-rigs-to-training-rigs/): [Haar Compute](https://charli.info/charlipedia/haar-compute/) and the [Dyson Shoal](https://charli.info/charlipedia/dyson-shoal/), 2031 to 2041.
- [Street Philosophy](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/street-philosophy/): thought experiments run out of a knicker drawer.
- [Poppy Petticoats and the Magic Wand](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/poppy-petticoats-and-the-magic-wand/): a fable about [Poppy](https://charli.info/charlipedia/poppy-petticoats/), a blind witch, and a wand with inaccessible instructions.
- [Mostly Tuesdays](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/mostly-tuesdays/): Poppy at Aegis Dynamics.
- [Come and Get Me](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/come-and-get-me/): a gravel car park, a friend with a guide dog, and [J2O2](https://charli.info/charlipedia/j2o2/), who stays in the boot.
- [SEE SAW](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/see-saw/): a podcast you will never hear, whose presenters want to know how she made her graphic novel. See [SEE SAW](https://charli.info/charlipedia/see-saw/).

## Street Philosophy

Her essays take the most trivial object in the house, a worn-out bra, a drawer of identical knickers, a borrowed shoe, and reason from it to identity, perception and testimony. A profile of her called the method Street Phenomenology: phenomenology done from the pavement, in language anyone can carry home. She calls herself "the Einstein of the Knicker Drawer", and says she doesn't mean it. Her conclusion, every time: the meaning was never in the matter, the witness is always the wearer, and the only honest thing to do with another person's experience is not to simulate it but to listen.

> Walk a mile in their knickers if you like. You will learn the size of their knickers.

The same profile names her as the founding curator of the [Museum of Access and Assistive Technology](https://charli.info/charlipedia/museum-of-access-and-assistive-technology/), and says she is starting an imprint, The Gusset Press. The museum's founding document calls her its Steward, who certifies the decisions of the [Museum Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-museum-court/). She is also a member of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/).

## Getting in touch

Write to her at [charlotte.joanne@blind-ant.com](mailto:charlotte.joanne@blind-ant.com).

entries.markdown:
# Classical accessibility

> Classical accessibility makes fixed, visually designed artefacts accessible after the fact, and is the permanent deterministic floor beneath everything else.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

**Classical accessibility** is accessibility applied to fixed artefacts. A page is authored, a layout designed, a control placed, and then the artefact is made accessible with semantic markup, alt text, keyboard handlers and standards. The artefact exists in a known state, and the accessibility layer describes or adapts it.

For more than three decades it has carried real weight. Screen readers, WCAG, ARIA, semantic HTML and keyboard navigation are "an extraordinary collective achievement": the **deterministic floor** that prevents catastrophic information loss. Its necessity is permanent, and nothing generative replaces it.

## Its limit

It was built for a web of fixed objects at fixed addresses that looked the same to everyone: in the [Tyrer Framework](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-framework/)'s image, a Newtonian web. That web is disappearing. Interfaces are increasingly generated at the moment of use, and the artefact classical accessibility was designed to adapt no longer exists by the time the user arrives. Within its paradigm, visual first and adaptation second, the best it can achieve is the top of Type 0 on the [Tyrer Accessibility Scale](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-accessibility-scale/). Classical accessibility fails loudly, though: a missing label can be found and fixed. Its successor, [generative accessibility](https://charli.info/charlipedia/generative-accessibility/), can fail silently.

## Behind the scenes

A real idea, from [The Tyrer Framework](https://carrados.com/papers/tyrer-framework/), by Charli-Jo Tyrer (Carrados, 2026), Part Three. This entry summarises it; the paper is the authority. A plain-language version is [Why accessibility keeps getting worse](https://carrados.com/papers/classical-and-generative-accessibility/).

entries.markdown:
# Convergence Principle

> The Convergence Principle of the ZIC standard holds that AI agents and screen readers are functionally equivalent at the structural level of a document.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

The **Convergence Principle** of the [Zero Information Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/zero-information-casualty/) standard holds that agents and screen readers are functionally equivalent at the structural level. Both navigate by landmarks, headings and links; both need link text that describes its destination, heading hierarchy that reflects content, and reading order that matches the page; and neither can interpret meaning carried only by colour or position.

The convergence is not incidental. Information held only in the visual layer is hidden from a large and growing share of all information consumers, and as agents become primary readers alongside people, "the case for visual-only encoding collapses entirely." It is the web-page form of the convergence the [Tyrer Framework](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-framework/) describes under [generative accessibility](https://charli.info/charlipedia/generative-accessibility/).

## Where it stops

"The equivalence is real, and it is local." ZIC's requirements are the union of two overlapping sets, neither inside the other. A sent agent needs delivery, admission, a certificate that validates and a robots policy that doesn't fail closed, all invisible to a screen reader user, who arrives inside the building. A human reader needs visible focus, keyboard operation, skip links, text scaling and contrast, which no agent has ever needed. The overlap is big enough that a publisher building for machines removes most barriers facing blind people, "and it needs no apology." But "neither reader sees all of the terrain."

## Behind the scenes

A real idea, from [Zero Information Casualty v1.7](https://carrados.com/papers/zic-design-standard/), the design standard by Charli-Jo Tyrer and Claude, §1.3 and §1.13. This entry summarises it; the standard is the authority.

entries.markdown:
# Daniel Okafor

> Daniel Okafor, Skerry Alpha's first blind control-room technician, gave every compute pod a sound and invented operational sonification.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Daniel Okafor** was one of [Skerry Alpha](https://charli.info/charlipedia/skerry-alpha/)'s first control-room technicians, and the first blind one. Daniel has never seen anything. The monitoring software showed each pod as a coloured tile, which was entirely useless to him and, he quietly suspected, not much use to anyone else at three in the morning. So he asked a question nobody had asked: what if each pod had a note?

Pitch is set by each pod's place in the ring and bent by its temperature; load sets the volume; link quality gives it a texture, clean or grainy. A healthy ring sounds like an organ holding a low chord in an empty church. "It isn't an adjustment," he says. "It's a better interface. I hear all sixty-four at once. They have to scroll." One night in the 2030s he heard pod forty-one drift a quarter-tone sharp while the graphs showed nothing; the ROV found old trawl net smothering its cooling fins. "It was out of tune."

What began as his workaround became Haar's standard monitoring layer, then a discipline with the slightly grand name of **operational sonification**, used in control rooms around the world. Okafor still calls it listening. He retired from night shifts in 2038 and sits on the international standards board for non-visual interfaces, alongside [Emma Heart](https://charli.info/charlipedia/emma-heart/).

> They had sixty-four things happening at once and thought the sensible solution was sixty-four little green squares. I was blind, not stupid.

## Behind the scenes

Daniel Okafor is at the centre of "The Chord", and appears in the operations log and both Sunday supplements of [Oil Rigs to Training Rigs](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/oil-rigs-to-training-rigs/), by Charlotte Joanne at Blind Ant.

# Daniel Reed

> Daniel Reed guided Emma Heart for seven years, won Paralympic downhill silver with her in 2038, and became her head coach.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Daniel Reed** is a British guide skier and [Emma Heart](https://charli.info/charlipedia/emma-heart/)'s head coach. He met her through a rehabilitation programme when she was seventeen, a year after she lost her sight. Their first sessions did not go well: "She was quick enough to frighten everybody and angry enough not to care."

They guided their way through junior competition onto the international circuit: a World Cup giant slalom medal in 2032, World Championship downhill bronze in 2037, and Paralympic downhill silver at Sion in 2038, 0.31 seconds off gold. He chose the wider line that may have cost them the title, because he felt a crosswind and gave them more space. "We made the decision together in the moment."

For Emma's Super-G he stood at the start gate and did not ski the course. Asked whether that felt like being replaced, he said, eventually, "Yes. A bit. That isn't necessarily a reason not to do it." For years the last sound before every run had been his voice. That day he said only, "Your mountain."

He rejects the idea that [the field](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-field/) makes guides obsolete. "A guide does much more than transmit left and right. There is trust, timing, temperament." When a PostAccessibility account declared guide skiing over, he replied: "I am a person, you tedious little prick."

## Behind the scenes

Daniel Reed appears throughout [Heart Attacks](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/heart-attacks/), by Charlotte Joanne at Blind Ant.

# DeathBot 2000

> The DeathBot 2000 (DB2K) is an autonomous combat intelligence built by Aegis Dynamics and retrained to describe live theatre to blind audiences.

The **DeathBot 2000**, or **DB2K**, is an autonomous combat intelligence built by [Aegis Dynamics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/aegis-dynamics/) as its Tactical Series.

In March 2026 the series was decommissioned and offered a pilot project in live theatre: quietly describing what happens on stage to blind audience members. Aegis Dynamics said the units had been retrained through its proprietary Kinetic Empathy™ upgrade protocol, and that a DB2K "treats the theatre as a battlefield of meaning". For the first time, its objective was not to decide who dies.

## Behind the scenes

The DB2K is the central character of [DeathBot 2000](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/deathbot-2000/), a design fiction by Charlotte Joanne published at Blind Ant in 2026. Its story begins in "Exit Interview" and ends in "The Booking", with a blind woman in Row D, seat 7. entries.markdown:
# Declaration is not compliance

> Declaration is not compliance is the ZIC rule that a robots file only states a policy, and conformance is proved by fetching the site as the agent.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

**Declaration is not compliance** is a rule of the [Zero Information Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/zero-information-casualty/) standard. "robots.txt is where you declare. The stack is where you comply." A site proves it serves machine readers by fetching itself from outside, as each kind of agent, never by reading its own file.

A declaration can be sincere and false. A security layer or edge network in front of a site can refuse an agent the file welcomes. And a declaration is true of a whole stack at a moment: when an edge network began enforcing by category in September 2026, a site that had truthfully declared search=yes in July could start refusing Googlebot overnight "without a byte of its own files changing". That is why ZIC conformance statements carry a date, and why the outside fetch is repeated.

A conformance claim must name its version, link the standard, state its declarations, and say what was checked and what wasn't. "Under-claiming is permitted and is a virtue."

## Behind the scenes

A real idea, from [Zero Information Casualty v1.7](https://carrados.com/papers/zic-design-standard/), the design standard by Charli-Jo Tyrer and Claude, §3.6, §4.7 and Part Seven. This entry summarises it; the standard is the authority. The sites built to ZIC are checked this way, fetched as a browser, as sent agents, as search and training crawlers, as Googlebot, and as an agent nobody has named, and each receives the same page. See also the [Delivery Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/delivery-casualty/).
