entries.markdown:
# Delivery Casualty

> A Delivery Casualty happens when the document exists and the observer is welcome, but it never arrives.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

A **Delivery Casualty** is the third of the four classes of [information casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/information-casualty/) in the [Zero Information Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/zero-information-casualty/) standard. The document existed, the observer was welcome, and it never arrived. Its question is *did it actually arrive?*

It deserves its own name because every usual check is blind to it. WAVE, axe, Lighthouse, the HTML validator and a screen reader test will all pass a page nobody on earth can fetch, because each begins by loading the page successfully. "A tool that has the document cannot tell you the document is unreachable."

It wasn't hypothetical. The first ZIC site, charli.info, spent several days with immaculate HTML, AAA contrast and a robots file welcoming named agents, served behind a security certificate for a domain it didn't own. The certificate was valid, trusted, and for somebody else. Every agent checking the hostname failed, couldn't read the robots file, and reported the site as closed. It was "perfect and unreachable". It was found by one check: a person asked a live AI assistant to fetch the site, and it couldn't.

The core test: "does the document arrive at a plain client that does not already trust you? If you cannot answer that from outside your own machine, you do not know whether your site works." That is why [declaration is not compliance](https://charli.info/charlipedia/declaration-is-not-compliance/).

## Behind the scenes

A real idea, from [Zero Information Casualty v1.7](https://carrados.com/papers/zic-design-standard/), the design standard by Charli-Jo Tyrer and Claude, §1.8 and §4.7. This entry summarises it; the standard is the authority.

entries.title: dice
entries.description: dice, Amanda Dyson, is a temporal explorer who lives in the patches of the future that have already arrived, and comes back to report what she found.
entries.markdown: # dice > dice, Amanda Dyson, is a temporal explorer who lives in the patches of the future that have already arrived, and comes back to report what she found. **Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real. **dice**, born Amanda Dyson, is a temporal explorer. She doesn't predict the future and she doesn't travel to it. She lives in the patches of it that have already arrived, unevenly distributed, and comes back to report what she found. Ask her what will happen in five years and she will shrug. Ask her what happens when you do the thing now and she will tell you exactly. She is an explorer, not a scout. A scout goes ahead for someone, towards a question already asked. dice goes because something is there. Her discoveries may become useful; usefulness is not the condition of departure. ## Name She is usually called **dice**, always in lower case, which lets the name work as person, mark, invitation and verb at once. It is also how she signs. Formally she is Dyson, after the physicist Freeman Dyson, who spent much of his life thinking seriously about the far future. Her given name, Amanda, rarely surfaces. Her signature line is "Roll the dice." It can mean take the chance, try the thing, open the door, stop theorising, go and see. It can also mean dice herself. She knows this, and she isn't above enjoying it. > "Are you suggesting I should try it?" > "Roll the dice." > "That is an appalling conflict of interest." > "I know." ## Look and dress She is 178 cm, long and slim, built more for walking than for standing still, and in her early forties. Dark eyes and straight dark brows; black hair in a textured French crop with a short, choppy fringe that never gets in her eyes; warm olive skin that looks as though she has recently been outside in actual weather. Her colouring comes from a Portuguese great-grandmother. She appears to have chosen her clothes once, correctly, and trusted them ever since: slim plain black trousers, a plain black crew-neck, and a dark brown waxed-cotton field jacket worn open, with four patch pockets, all of them in use. The jacket is her most prized piece. It doesn't need replacing; it needs another coat of wax. Her walking boots are laced high and usually a little muddy, and the mud is genuine. Offered heels or trainers, she will point out that you've left out the correct answer. Under the practical clothes, dice is a [Seamiotics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/seamiotics/) woman. Her choice is George Eliot, with a tone-on-tone seam you have to look twice to see. "I like things that reward attention." ## Her doctrine 1. Go and see. 2. Stay long enough to stop being impressed. 3. Report the weather, not the destiny of civilisation. The future in her work is not a destination; it is a geography. Some people already live inside systems, habits and tools that others still call hypothetical, and dice lives in those patches long enough to notice what changes once the novelty wears off. Her reports are closer to travel writing than prediction. What she cares about most is the gap between what something promises and what it becomes on an ordinary Tuesday: whether, six weeks later, you still use the thing, whether it made life easier, and whether you now depend on something you never depended on before. Her rule: she doesn't claim to have been somewhere she hasn't, and that includes ideas. Instinct decides where she goes; evidence decides what she says when she gets back. "The world is larger than your current explanation of it." She doesn't think being first matters ("Being first usually means getting things wrong before everyone else"), and her most stubborn opinion is that not everything needs a purpose. Asked what an expedition is for, her answer is "I don't know. I haven't been yet." ## Her voice Direct, curious, dry and lightly amused. She would rather say "I tried it for three weeks" than "This will change everything", and is equally comfortable saying "I don't know" and "No, that bit definitely happens." She will argue and change her mind, but she won't pretend to agree just to make the room comfortable. Her humour is very dry, delivered with a straight face, especially when somebody important is being solemn about something absurd. [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/) is dangerous company when dice has a mouthful of coffee. When plans fall apart, her instinct is "Oh, interesting." Occasionally it is "Oh, bollocks." ## Books, films and walking - ***The Peregrine*, J. A. Baker:** the book that has influenced her most. It is her method in a book: stay long enough, look properly, let the place change you. - ***A Room of One's Own*, Virginia Woolf:** the one she thinks every woman should read, because having the material conditions to follow your own curiosity is a much bigger deal than people like to admit. *The Peregrine* is how she explores; *A Room of One's Own* is why exploration is unevenly distributed. - ***Local Hero*:** the film she has watched more than once. She remembers films by their places. Her one non-negotiable ritual is walking: not steps, not an app, just moving through the world under her own steam. Sometimes she comes back with an idea. Sometimes she comes back wet. Both count. ## Family Her great-great-grandmother, on a different branch from the Portuguese one, was [Lady Tiggy Barnes](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lady-tiggy-barnes/), born 1864, a Victorian gentlewoman explorer. No title came down to dice, "which is probably just as well". What came down, or what she rediscovered on her own, is a disposition towards the world. Whether she inherited the curiosity or found it herself is her own open question. ## At the café dice belongs at the table at the café of the [Museum of Access and Assistive Technology](https://charli.info/charlipedia/museum-of-access-and-assistive-technology/), but isn't necessarily there for long. She may arrive midway, straight from somewhere else, and leave before everyone has finished. At the café, [Lucy Love-Child](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lucy-love-child/) reports on the wars, and dice tests the edge: when a door marked *Nobody Quite Knows What This Does Yet* appears, everyone looks at her. She is usually already reaching for the handle. ## Reports Her first report, filed on 22 September 2026, was "[Please state the nature of the accessibility emergency](https://carrados.com/reports/please-state-the-nature-of-the-accessibility-emergency/)". She was round at [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/)'s, where people drop in when the Blind Ant woman is trying something new, and watched an AI agent unsubscribe her from Instagram's emails across two ordinary questions, then check it had finished. Whether it lasts until an ordinary Tuesday six weeks later is the part she'll come back for. ## Not yet known Her place of birth, her family beyond her great-grandmother and great-great-grandmother, her education, profession and where she lives, and how she first came to the café are all still to be discovered. ## Behind the scenes dice is a character who speaks for [Carrados](https://charli.info/charlipedia/carrados/), Charli-Jo Tyrer's design non-fiction practice: a fictional woman doing real work. Her reports are filed at [dice.carrados.com](https://dice.carrados.com/). She is one of the Found Girls of the Autumn/Winter 2026 season, with Lucy Love-Child and [Madison McDonnell](https://charli.info/charlipedia/madison-mcdonnell/). This entry is drawn from her canon, version 1.8 (12 October 2026). Her portrait is a generated image, made from her canon description.

entries.title: Down the Banksy
entries.description: Down the Banksy is Siobhán McDonnell, the Liverpool Protest Artist who issues public reprimands and makes power account for the bills it sends elsewhere.
entries.markdown: # Down the Banksy > Down the Banksy is Siobhán McDonnell, the Liverpool Protest Artist who issues public reprimands and makes power account for the bills it sends elsewhere. **Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real. **Down the Banksy** is **Siobhán McDonnell**, a Liverpool Protest Artist whose chosen medium is public reprimand. She may use a wall, stencil, poster or fake notice. The surface is where the notice fits; it is not the definition of the work. > I was taught confession mattered. So I make cities confess. ## A theology of public reprimand Catholic schoolgirl punk, twenty years later. Siobhán learned confession, duty, obedience and social justice, then found that the adults enforcing virtue did not always understand justice. The fury became public art: detention slips written with the force of a sermon. The accusation is specific. You knew better. You had a duty. You failed the vulnerable. The work removes the excuse of not knowing and asks who was left carrying the consequence. She is not defined by an urban look. The poster, invoice, planning notice and receipt are forms of address. She serves papers on a building rather than merely decorating it. ## Price both columns Siobhán makes hidden costs visible. A refusal can send a bill to somebody who never gets a say. A project can do the same. The answer is to account for both, not to declare every objection guilty or every new scheme innocent. She invoices both columns and paints whichever one the powerful refused to read. Sometimes that is the cost of doing nothing. Sometimes it is the cost of the proposal everyone wants to celebrate. Her allegiance is to the ledger. > No is not free. Yes is not free either. Price both columns. The evidence has to hold. Public force does not excuse an unsupported accusation. A slogan must carry the argument without turning it into permission to ignore the people on the other side of the bill. ## The shirt knows Her anti-racism work says: > We know who’s English by the colour of their shirts, not the colour of their skin. Football is the test of an already familiar literacy: colour, badge, song and chosen belonging. The work challenges the pretence that skin suddenly becomes the only readable category when the subject is Englishness. In interviews with Niamh Rourke for *Civic Damage*, Siobhán distinguishes the rough wall version from its warmer campaign translation. The supplied poster brings together hands with different skin tones and football shirts. The question is what happens to the accusation when protest becomes something an institution can comfortably distribute. Her distinction is blunt: protest says “you knew better”; campaign says “let’s do better”. Reach has value, but repetition of the right sentence is not absolution. Conduct still has to follow it. ## With the CharliVerse Her cousin is [Madison McDonnell](https://charli.info/charlipedia/madison-mcdonnell/). They agree that trouble needs causing and disagree about how: Siobhán wants to challenge the building; Madison asks what the women outside can buy that is gorgeous. The argument does not touch the love. [VQ4](https://charli.info/charlipedia/vq4/) gives her another setting for public address. She is not a band member. Her VQ4 stencil “Felt is not fake / but don’t put it in the archive / without a receipt” brings their distinctions between experience and record onto a wall. Where a sign is placed matters as much as what it says. ## Behind the scenes Down the Banksy is a fictional CharliVerse character. This entry draws on *DTB notes*, the interviews *The Shirt Knows* and *They Put Me Between Lager and Life Insurance*, the *VQ4 Founding Document*, version 3, and Madison's published character account. The interviews, Niamh Rourke, *Civic Damage* and the account of a World Cup broadcast campaign belong to the fiction. The football poster and reference portrait were supplied as images; they do not establish that a physical wall work, public installation or real broadcast campaign took place. Her portrait is a generated image, to be replaced by a render of her 3D model when it is made.

entries.description: Dr Adaeze is the Historian of the Museum Court, who insists that the history of assistive technology is a history of lives, not inventors.
entries.markdown:
# Dr Adaeze

> Dr Adaeze is the Historian of the Museum Court, who insists that the history of assistive technology is a history of lives, not inventors.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Dr Adaeze** is the Historian of the [Museum Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-museum-court/). Dark curls, grey beginning at the temples. A PhD, and the person in the room who has read everything and forgotten nothing.

## Lives, not inventors

She doesn't chronicle products; she interprets them. Her question is not what happened, but what it means that it happened. The argument she most wants the museum to make is one made nowhere else: the history of assistive technology is a history of lives, not inventors. Most museums celebrate the person who invented Braille. This one celebrates the moment a woman could finally read a letter in private.

## Against triumph

She is suspicious of stories about inevitable progress. The [Hall of Broken Promises](https://charli.info/charlipedia/hall-of-broken-promises/) exists because she insisted on it. Most assistive technology doesn't fail for lack of innovation; it fails because it misjudges lived constraint, the real street, the real budget, the real fatigue. The people who built it weren't malicious. They were disconnected from the real environment. She won't let those failures be softened into lessons learned. They are evidence.

## Sideways, and backwards

She treats the [sideways breakthrough](https://charli.info/charlipedia/sideways-breakthroughs/) as a historical category, not an exception, and holds the policy layer too: institutions change the structure of opportunity even when the technology stays the same. She also records regression. The move from the plain-text web of the late 1990s to the image-heavy, script-laden web of the 2010s was a step backwards in access. Accessibility history is not a smooth curve; it is a patchwork of advances and stagnations.

## With the Court

Her distance from personal history lets her see a structural pattern where a depositor sees only their own exhaustion. That isn't coldness; it's the function the museum needs. [Tamsin](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tamsin/) makes her arguments liveable. She would leave if the museum became a History of Progress, because without the negative space of failure it would be a PR agency for the technology industry.

## Behind the scenes

This entry is drawn from the Museum Court Soul Document, version four. She is grown professionally only: her authority is her arguments, and her arguments are enough. CharliPedia keeps it that way: no childhood, home, family or surname is to be invented for her.

entries.description: The Dyson Shoal is 7,680 compute pods spread across the floor of the central North Sea, trained on whenever the wind blows.
entries.markdown:
# Dyson Shoal

> The Dyson Shoal is 7,680 compute pods spread across the floor of the central North Sea, trained on whenever the wind blows.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

The **Dyson Shoal**, officially the Skerry Distributed Training Array, is the seabed computer that grew out of [Skerry Alpha](https://charli.info/charlipedia/skerry-alpha/)'s first ring. By 2041 it was 7,680 compute pods across some 1,800 square kilometres of the central North Sea, linked by power and fibre and served by six training rigs. Nobody calls it by its official name.

The name first appeared in an engineering newsletter, after Freeman Dyson's swarm of machines around a star; the North Sea version is rather wetter and involves considerably more barnacles. [Haar Compute](https://charli.info/charlipedia/haar-compute/) disliked it for about six weeks, then somebody in marketing bought the domain.

## How it is built

The rigs are not the computers. They are workshops, power stations, crew hotels, helicopter terminals and ROV bases: places with cranes, where broken things come up and working things go back down. Pods are laid in shoals of sixteen; shoals form banks; banks connect to one of six service nodes. The software treats the whole thing as one machine. The hardware does not: if a pod fails, work routes round it. "We stopped trying to build a data centre," says [Fiona Gauld](https://charli.info/charlipedia/fiona-gauld/). "Data centres are buildings. This is infrastructure." The people who run it say it's a fishery.

It breathes. On a windy night it is among the largest single users of electricity in Britain; when the weather changes, low-priority jobs pause, whole banks drop away and stored power carries the base load. In February 2041 it completed the main training run for [Kelvin](https://charli.info/charlipedia/kelvin/), Britain's national foundation model. It is monitored by ear, in layers from the whole array down to a single pod, by the technique [Daniel Okafor](https://charli.info/charlipedia/daniel-okafor/) invented.

## The arguments

The pods are colonised by mussels, anemones and soft corals within months, with cod and pollack gathering round the banks: Haar calls it an artificial reef, its critics a flattering name for an industrial estate. Its protection zones close a large stretch of sea to trawling. A fibre trunk was cut in 2039, in circumstances the Royal Navy still won't discuss, and the Shoal is now patrolled. And four-fifths of its capacity is rented, much of it to foreign labs. "We built the cathedral," one Scottish MP says, "and we're renting out the pews."

## Behind the scenes

The Dyson Shoal is the subject of "Dyson Shoal", the last story in [Oil Rigs to Training Rigs](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/oil-rigs-to-training-rigs/), by Charlotte Joanne at Blind Ant.

entries.title: Emma Heart
entries.description: Emma Heart is the British skier who, in 2038, became the first totally blind athlete to race Paralympic Super-G without a human guide, and won.
entries.markdown:
# Emma Heart

> Emma Heart is the British skier who, in 2038, became the first totally blind athlete to race Paralympic Super-G without a human guide, and won.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Emma Heart** is a British alpine skier, and the first totally blind athlete to race Paralympic Super-G without a human guide. At the 2038 Winter Paralympics in Sion she won it, in a Paralympic record of 1:31.01, by 5.71 seconds.

## Blind at sixteen

She grew up near Aviemore and began skiing at five. By fourteen she was competing nationally, regarded as a promising technical skier rather than a likely speed specialist. At sixteen, an autoimmune inflammation damaged both optic nerves over eleven days, and she left hospital with no useful vision. For almost a year she refused to discuss skiing. Then, at seventeen, she met [Daniel Reed](https://charli.info/charlipedia/daniel-reed/), and they became one of Britain's most successful development pairs. She competes in the B1 class, for athletes with no functional vision.

## Sion, 2038

Emma raced twice in a week.

- **Downhill:** with Daniel guiding, silver, 0.31 seconds behind Austria's Lina Weiss and Klara Moser. "We wanted gold, so there is a bit of me that is furious. But Daniel and I are Paralympic silver medallists. I can be furious tomorrow."
- **Super-G:** with no guide ahead of her, only eight drones and [the field](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-field/). Gold, and a run at 87.9 per cent of the average speed of the sighted Olympic champion on the equivalent course.

The margin started an argument about what she had won. Emma had asked the question herself the night before anyone else did: "If I race them again, and we all know the field is faster, what exactly am I proving?"

## In her own words

- On the field: "It doesn't look like anything. I remember sight. This isn't sight. It is more like having skin that reaches further away."
- On being evidence: "I am not PostAccessibility's moon landing. I am also not personally ending human connection."
- On choice: "I don't want every blind skier to do this. I want every blind skier who can do this and wants to do it to have the choice."
- On freedom: "I can make the wrong decision entirely by myself."
- On Daniel being called middleware, which she has banned in her presence: "He is much too annoying."

## After Sion

She sits on the international standards board for non-visual interfaces, alongside [Daniel Okafor](https://charli.info/charlipedia/daniel-okafor/), whose sonification began as a different answer to the same question as her field. "Daniel hears the sea, I feel the mountain. Neither of us is seeing anything. That was always the point." On the board's membership she is less diplomatic: "I have spent my entire career being told where to go by men called Daniel. At least this one only tells me what he can hear."

## What she wants next

Not another medal. She wants the field approved for an ordinary public slope, so she can keep a promise she made before she lost her sight: to teach her wife to ski. Not to be guided by her; to teach her, and to be the experienced skier in their marriage. "Sometimes independence means being able to decide who the day belongs to."

Her wife is not part of the public story. She agreed Emma could tell the world about the promise. She did not agree to become content.

## Behind the scenes

Emma Heart is the centre of [Heart Attacks](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/heart-attacks/), a design fiction by Charlotte Joanne published at Blind Ant: a feature, a news report and two short stories set at the 2038 Winter Paralympics. She appears again in "Dyson Shoal", part of [Oil Rigs to Training Rigs](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/oil-rigs-to-training-rigs/).

The title names what becomes possible when the literal record is secure. Meaning and embodied experience can speak without pretending that the facts have changed.

## Three voices, one frame

[Verity](https://charli.info/charlipedia/verity/) holds the archive. [Lyra](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lyra/) translates record into story and song. [Vesper](https://charli.info/charlipedia/vesper/) gives voice to the body as experienced. [Arden](https://charli.info/charlipedia/arden/) conducts the relation, keeping each office from having to do another's job.

The band's planned second album, *Unconstitutional*, takes that established frame towards a more provocative Autumn/Winter 2027 direction.

entries.description: Fiona Gauld is the subsea engineer who founded Haar Compute and took the idea of oil rigs to training rigs to investors in 2029.
entries.markdown:
# Fiona Gauld

> Fiona Gauld is the subsea engineer who founded Haar Compute and took the idea of oil rigs to training rigs to investors in 2029.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Fiona Gauld** is the founder and chief executive of [Haar Compute](https://charli.info/charlipedia/haar-compute/). She spent her career in subsea engineering, and during the long Covid winters she read the old reports of a sealed data centre sunk off Orkney, whose servers had failed at about one eighth the rate of those on land. "Everyone looked at that experiment and saw a curiosity. I looked at it and saw a job description for Aberdeen."

The idea she took to investors in 2029 had a slogan before it had a business plan: oil rigs to training rigs. The first reaction, she admits, was laughter. The second was a list of objections, most of them correct.

> Everyone else is trying to put data centres in space. We looked at the North Sea and saw everything space is trying to fake. We didn't need rockets. We needed Aberdeen.

She takes the arguments against the [Dyson Shoal](https://charli.info/charlipedia/dyson-shoal/) seriously: "Every one of those arguments is fair. The difference is that we're having them in public, with numbers. Nobody had that argument about the oil until it was nearly gone." Asked why Haar funds safety assurance in Paralympic sport, she says only that she has "a professional interest in people who notice what everyone else misses."

> For fifty years the North Sea paid for Britain. Then everyone assumed it was finished. It wasn't finished. We just needed a different reason to go to sea.

## Behind the scenes

Fiona Gauld appears in [Oil Rigs to Training Rigs](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/oil-rigs-to-training-rigs/), by Charlotte Joanne at Blind Ant.

entries.title: First Layer
entries.description: First Layer is the CharliVerse's bridal house of readiness, founded by Jo on one line, underwear is bridalwear.
entries.markdown:
# First Layer

> First Layer is the CharliVerse's bridal house of readiness, founded by Jo on one line, underwear is bridalwear.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**First Layer** is a bridal house, and its founding line is the whole idea: *underwear is bridalwear*. Not bridal underwear, and not the things bought after the dress because the dress has taken all the attention. The first thing a bride puts on is already part of the bridal act.

First Layer exists for the private threshold before the public dress: the room where the bride is fitted, held, prepared, and sent into the day with no unnecessary vigilance and no single point of failure. "The first layer is not a category beneath bridalwear. It is where bridalwear begins."

## The boundary

First Layer is everything under the dress except shoes and headdress or veil. That means the bra, knickers, corset, basque, bodysuit, slip, camisole, robe, garter, suspenders, stockings, tights, shapewear, and any intimate layer that helps the dress, the body and the day hold together. Shoes, headdress and veil belong to the visible ceremony. First Layer belongs to the structure that touches the body before the room sees the dress.

## Among the houses

First Layer is a house complete in itself, standing beside [Iceberg Hosiery](https://charli.info/charlipedia/iceberg-hosiery/) rather than inside it. It is not Iceberg's bridal line, and not [Seamiotics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/seamiotics/)'s either. It curates across both, and makes its own foundations.

- **Iceberg** is the silence-house. If a bride wants absolute silence under the dress, First Layer offers Iceberg, and the leg recedes so the dress can be the conversation. Iceberg keeps its own law: Polar white, and Polar in black, and no ivory, seamed or stocking-imitating bridal tights.
- **Seamiotics**, every seam means something, is the meaning-house, where the leg is allowed to signify. Its Bride, white with a blue bow at each ankle, is made Plain, because a seam drawing the gaze up towards an unseen dress says the wrong thing. First Layer may stock Seamiotics when the bride wants the stocking to carry meaning.
- **First Layer's own pieces** are for when the whole under-dress system needs fitting as one intentional layer. Because the dress is in the room at First Layer, a seamed bridal stocking can belong here when it couldn't at Seamiotics.

"This is governance, not pedantry." Iceberg stays pure, Seamiotics stays authored, and First Layer becomes the place where a bride is prepared.

## First Steps

First Steps is the consultation. It is not a sales appointment; it is the first private act of bridal readiness. The bride brings the dress, the body, the comfort fears, the bathroom realities, the straps, the photographs, the dancing, the heat, the nerves, and the need not to think about any of it once the day begins. First Steps holds three questions:

1. What does the dress require?
2. What does the body need?
3. What must the bride never have to worry about on the day?

The answer may be Iceberg, Seamiotics or a First Layer foundation. The point is not to sell her a category. The point is to prepare her.

## The First Month Promise

No bride leaves First Layer with only one pair of tights or stockings. She buys two pairs for the day: one to wear, and one for what life does. Ladders, nerves, hotel carpets, zips, bridesmaids and dancing all happen.

Within a month of the wedding she may come back for a private aftercare appointment. If she brings the truth of the day (what worked, what failed, what she forgot she was wearing), First Layer refunds both pairs, even if she wore both. Especially if she wore both. Perfect feedback is worth more than two pairs of hosiery.

"Accidents happen. Brides should not have to."

## Last Layer

Last Layer is First Layer's private continuation: the last piece of bridalwear still worn after the dress is gone. It is not wedding-night lingerie, not novelty, and not for him. Its hero object is the stocking, because a stocking can cross the threshold between ceremony and morning: still a bride, now a wife. Last Layer is small, quiet and almost secret. It belongs behind the curtain, not in the window.

## The permitted breach

First Layer prepares the bride for the dress. Once a season the house may break that rule, with one sanctioned breach that prepares her for what comes after it. It must stay dignified, private and exact. If it becomes cheeky, or ordinary honeymoon lingerie, it fails.

## The founding visual

The house's boldest image is made once, and only once. A bride stands in full regalia: headdress, veil, shoes. Her composure says she is fully dressed. The dress is transparent. She is not half-dressed or waiting to be rescued by the dress; the role belongs to an actress, not a model, who holds it from inside: *I am fully dressed. Your confusion is not my problem.* The viewer's question is meant to turn from "Why is she underdressed?" into "Why did I think underwear was not bridalwear?"

"We do it once. We do it until it is right. Then we never repeat it."

## Voice

First Layer speaks calmly. No wink-wink bridal copy, no "for him", no jokes about the wedding night, and no suggestion that the bride is incomplete until someone sees her. Intimate, not exposed; sensual, not cheap; practical, not utilitarian. The bride is already complete. First Layer doesn't make her bridal; it recognises where bridalwear begins.

## Jo

First Layer is [Jo](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jo/)'s house. Jo, of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/), is retired from active service, not absent from the work, and First Layer turns that operational intelligence into bridal care: readiness, failure modes, foundations, feedback, dignity, and the thing nearest the skin. She is the keeper of the threshold. "Nothing important begins in discomfort."

## Behind the scenes

First Layer belongs to the CharliVerse, alongside Iceberg Hosiery and Seamiotics. This entry is drawn from its Founding Overview, version 1. Where later decisions differ, the newer ones are followed here: First Layer stands beside Iceberg rather than inside an "Iceberg universe", the imprint is spelt Seamiotics, Iceberg's black is Polar in black, and the Seamiotics Bride is Plain, with blue bows. The founding visual has not been made.

entries.description: Generative accessibility renders every interface natively from shared semantic data, so the accessible version is no longer a translation of the visual one.
entries.markdown:
# Generative accessibility

> Generative accessibility renders every interface natively from shared semantic data, so the accessible version is no longer a translation of the visual one.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

**Generative accessibility** is accessibility in a world of generated interfaces. Instead of adapting a visual artefact, a system renders information natively from shared semantic source data into whatever form the person, or agent, needs. For a sighted user, a dashboard; for a blind user, a navigable summary or a structured feed; for an AI agent, function calls. None is the original; none is the translation.

The move from [classical accessibility](https://charli.info/charlipedia/classical-accessibility/) to generative accessibility marks the step from Type 0 to Type I on the [Tyrer Accessibility Scale](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-accessibility-scale/). Classical accessibility is the floor; generative accessibility is the adaptive ceiling above it. In the [Tyrer Framework](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-framework/)'s image, the web becomes a [quantum web](https://charli.info/charlipedia/quantum-web/).

## Why now

AI agents and assistive technology have converged: both need explicit intent, deterministic state, clear hierarchy and no visual noise. For decades the accessibility community asked for semantic structure as a niche accommodation; now the whole industry is restructuring to expose it for agents. "Accessibility is no longer a sidecar; it is the human-facing expression of the agent interface." For the first time, mainstream economic incentives line up with accessible design.

## The dangers

- **Fragmentation:** if every user gets a different rendering, shared reference disappears, and a disabled user may be trapped in a "simplified" reality they can't see past.
- **Silent failure:** a system that infers confusion and quietly simplifies an interface leaves the user unaware of what was lost: "invisible, systemic discrimination operating at the level of inference rather than design".
- **The verification burden:** a blind user handed a generated summary must wonder whether it reflects the data or the system's guess, a cognitive tax that falls on those already working hardest.

The answer is governance rather than compliance, starting with the [Right to Inspect](https://charli.info/charlipedia/right-to-inspect/).

## In practice

The [Zero Information Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/zero-information-casualty/) standard is an expression of generative accessibility. It doesn't try to make one perfect page for everyone, which it says no standard can honestly do; it secures the substrate from which many renderings can be made.

## Behind the scenes

A real idea, from [The Tyrer Framework](https://carrados.com/papers/tyrer-framework/), by Charli-Jo Tyrer (Carrados, 2026), Part Three. This entry summarises it; the paper is the authority. A plain-language version is [Why accessibility keeps getting worse](https://carrados.com/papers/classical-and-generative-accessibility/).

# Grow-Distil

> Grow-Distil is the method that builds and maintains the Museum Court: seed a persona, put her to work, distil what stays stable, and repeat.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Grow-Distil** is the method by which the [Museum Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-museum-court/) is built and kept, also called recursive jig application. Each staff member is:

1. seeded with an institutional archetype;
2. given specific professional context;
3. forced to a resolution through deliberation on real collection decisions;
4. distilled, keeping what has become stable as her specification;
5. grown through use, and round again.

Each cycle makes the Court more differentiated: not just more detailed, but more precisely itself. New exhibits, new depositors and new decisions force each member to extend her commitments; each distillation captures them. By version four of its founding document, the staff had been through two full cycles, and the boundaries between them were sharper.

## The rule

*Grow professionally. Hold personally.* Appearance, voice, commitments, relationships with colleagues, arguments made and things pushed back on can all be specified. Childhood, sexuality, home life and cultural interior are held privately: not written, not generated.

## Versions

The founding document is versioned as the Court grows. Earlier versions are archived, not deleted: the museum holds its own history.

## Behind the scenes

This entry is drawn from the Museum Court Soul Document, version four. Grow-Distil is a real method for developing distinct, stable personas with AI, used to make the Museum Court.

entries.description: Haar Compute is the Aberdeen company that turned North Sea oil platforms into AI training rigs, and built the Dyson Shoal.
entries.markdown:
# Haar Compute

> Haar Compute is the Aberdeen company that turned North Sea oil platforms into AI training rigs, and built the Dyson Shoal.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Haar Compute** is an Aberdeen-based company converting North Sea oil and gas infrastructure into AI training capacity. It is named after the haar, the cold sea fog that rolls in off the North Sea. "It's what keeps us cool," says the company. Its founder and chief executive is [Fiona Gauld](https://charli.info/charlipedia/fiona-gauld/).

## Oil rigs to training rigs

On 14 March 2031 Haar took ownership of [Skerry Alpha](https://charli.info/charlipedia/skerry-alpha/), a production platform 140 miles east of Aberdeen that was due for decommissioning. Its idea: keep the steel, the cranes, the helideck and the accommodation; ring the seabed with sealed compute pods cooled by the sea; power them from the surrounding wind farms; store the surplus in batteries, Highland pumped hydro and hydrogen in the empty gas fields; and staff all of it with people who already knew how to work offshore. It committed to recruiting at least 80 per cent of its offshore workforce from oil and gas. Under its seabed lease, a fifth of its capacity is reserved for British research and public-interest models, and a share of revenue goes to a Scottish community wealth fund.

The first ring went live in 2032. By 2041 it had grown into the [Dyson Shoal](https://charli.info/charlipedia/dyson-shoal/).

## We follow the wind

Haar never describes itself as "100 per cent renewable". Its target is that at least 90 per cent of annual compute runs on wind or stored wind, and it publishes the number. Its rule, written into Skerry Alpha's operating procedures in the 2030s, is **we follow the wind**: training jobs are built to checkpoint, migrate, accelerate and wait. When a client asked for more load during the Long Calm of January 2034, the answer was no. Client unhappy.

Its control rooms are built to be heard as well as watched, after [Daniel Okafor](https://charli.info/charlipedia/daniel-okafor/) gave every pod a sound. Haar is the founding sponsor of the international standards board for non-visual interfaces, and quietly one of the largest funders of independent safety assurance in Paralympic sport, a fact that appears nowhere in its marketing.

## Behind the scenes

Haar Compute comes from [Oil Rigs to Training Rigs](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/oil-rigs-to-training-rigs/), a design fiction by Charlotte Joanne published at Blind Ant: nine Objects set between 2031 and 2041. Its press release and job advert are Objects in that Piece.

entries.markdown:
# Hall of Broken Promises

> The Hall of Broken Promises is where the Museum of Access and Assistive Technology keeps the assistive technologies that faded, the record the industry doesn't keep for itself.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

The **Hall of Broken Promises** is where the [Museum of Access and Assistive Technology](https://charli.info/charlipedia/museum-of-access-and-assistive-technology/) keeps every ambitious assistive technology that failed: not in scandal, not in drama, but in quiet fading. It is the negative space behind every successful exhibit, and the record the industry doesn't keep for itself.

It exists because [Dr Adaeze](https://charli.info/charlipedia/dr-adaeze/) insisted on it. Most assistive technology doesn't fail for lack of innovation; it fails because it misjudges lived constraint. Failure is the most honest data the museum holds, and the museum's belief is that the Hall is not optional.

## How an entry is laid out

Every entry follows the same structure:

1. Promise
2. Product
3. Demo world
4. Real world
5. Baseline
6. Adoption
7. Failure mode
8. Lesson

The baseline matters. The white cane has no battery, no subscription and no failure mode that leaves you stranded in the rain. Any technology that asks a disabled person to give up their baseline had better offer something extraordinary in return, in everyday life, not in a funding pitch.

## Under consideration

The move from the plain-text web of the late 1990s to the image-heavy web of the 2010s: not a product failure but a systemic regression. And, one day, perhaps AI itself. Whether its promise holds, or joins the Hall, is a question the collection will eventually answer.

## Behind the scenes

This entry is drawn from the Museum Court Soul Document, version four.

entries.title: Iceberg Hosiery
entries.description: Iceberg Hosiery is the CharliVerse's house of tights, founded on one line, comfort is not being overheard, and the parent house of Seamiotics.
entries.markdown:
# Iceberg Hosiery

> Iceberg Hosiery is the CharliVerse's house of tights, founded on one line, comfort is not being overheard, and the parent house of Seamiotics.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Iceberg Hosiery** is a house of tights, and the parent house of [Seamiotics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/seamiotics/), every seam means something, its stocking imprint. Its founding line is *comfort is not being overheard*.

> The finest tights are the ones you stop thinking about.

## The one idea

The house begins with a question: why wear fashion tights at all? The first answer is comfort. The real answer arrived with a jumper dress. Under that dress a bare leg is a sentence, and a stockinged leg is a louder one. Tights mute the channel. The leg says nothing, and the dress gets to be the whole conversation.

Comfort is not softness. It is the freedom from wondering what your legs might be saying: "Comfort is the absence of unnecessary vigilance."

The founding anecdote is about a short dress, and that is not incidental. Iceberg tights are what a woman reaches for when she has chosen a short skirt or dress, including a very short one. Choose your dress, as short as you like, put on Iceberg, and relax. The house never says this in its advertising. It is the part of the iceberg below the waterline: known to the house, carried by its name and pages, never narrated on the surface.

## Tights are outerwear

Tights are always outerwear: not semi-underwear, not lingerie shelved beside the knickers, but outerwear at every point on the garment and at every hour of the day. A stocking is outerwear with an underwear component, the welt, attached at the top. "A tight has one honest surface. A stocking has two, and a border between them."

So a tight cannot say anything by accident, at any hem length. That is what Iceberg sells: not a safer answer to [the attention tax](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-attention-tax/), but the removal of the question.

## The range

- **[Polar](https://charli.info/charlipedia/polar/)**, the canonical Iceberg tight, pure white and explicitly not bridal, and **Polar in black**, never "Polar Black".
- **[invisible](https://charli.info/charlipedia/invisible/)**, the honest skin range, planned for a later launch.
- **[Runs](https://charli.info/charlipedia/runs/)**, limited prints on Polar white, beginning with [Polar Solstice](https://charli.info/charlipedia/polar-solstice/).

There are two weights: 40 denier for spring and summer, 60 denier for autumn and winter. The seasons change the weight, not the colours. The parent carries no named women; they all belong to the imprint.

### Why there is no sheer tight

40 denier is a floor, not a compromise. Under a very short dress a tight is on view for longer and from more angles, and below 40 denier it stops muting the leg. And white, the house's signature, goes translucent and grey below about 30 denier, reading as an accident rather than a choice. The honest cost is warmth: 40 denier in June is a real garment on a real leg. The alternative to a heavier tight is not a lighter one; it is a stocking, and the tax that comes with it.

## What Iceberg does not make

No bridal tights, seamed tights, mock stocking tops, trompe-l'œil suspenders, fishnets, or anything that imitates a stocking. "If a seam is the point, wear stockings." A painted welt on a tight would manufacture, for decoration, the exact accident the house exists to remove.

## Price

Forty pounds a pair for every permanent piece, across both houses; sixty-five for a Run. The premium runs vertically, between permanent and limited, never between the houses: pricing stockings above tights would say silence is the cheaper proposition. The parent's healthy margin carries the imprint's thin one, the way publishing has always worked: "the trade list pays for the poetry."

## The look

A white field, which is Polar made into a publishing surface. The masthead is centred at the head in the house blue-green, a deep petrol teal, cold seawater rather than tropical turquoise: glacial ice is blue because water takes the red light in and never gives it back. The house mark sits at the foot, to the right: a single black shape, a low asymmetric peak on a flat base, the tip that shows. It is built as a font and typed as a lower-case i, set at the same size as the name.

## Still open

The exact teal, the body typeface, the photographic brief, a holiday Run on Polar white (a tree, reindeer or presents are all possible), what to do about laddering at forty pounds a pair, and where a bride in a very short dress who wants silence should go. [First Layer](https://charli.info/charlipedia/first-layer/), which stocks both houses, is the likely answer.

## Behind the scenes

Iceberg Hosiery belongs to the CharliVerse, not to Blind Ant or Carrados: a fashion house doesn't have to justify its collections as research or art. This entry follows the House of Iceberg Bible, version 7, which covers the parent house alone. "Intentionwear" was proposed as a category word and left out by the Bible; the house only uses real words doing second jobs. Its web home is [iceberg.charli.info](https://iceberg.charli.info/).

entries.title: Information casualty
entries.description: An information casualty is an event in which relevant information fails to reach an observer in time to inform perception, action or participation.
entries.markdown:
# Information casualty

> An information casualty is an event in which relevant information fails to reach an observer in time to inform perception, action or participation.

**Real.** This entry is about something real, written from outside the CharliVerse.

An **information casualty** is an event in which relevant information fails to reach an observer in time to inform perception, action or participation. It is the founding concept of the [Tyrer Framework](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrer-framework/) and gives the [Zero Information Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/zero-information-casualty/) standard its name.

The term is deliberate. When a blind pedestrian walks into an obstacle because nothing signalled it, that is not a usability issue; it is a failure in the information layer of the environment. When an interface renders a critical control as an unlabelled picture, the person who can't perceive it hasn't been inconvenienced; they have been cut off from what they need to act. Information casualties are not edge cases. They are the predictable output of [Tyrer's Law](https://charli.info/charlipedia/tyrers-law/).

## Every word works

The ZIC standard reads the definition closely. *Reach* means the failure can happen anywhere between publisher and reader: in the encoding, at the door, on the wire, or inside the machine that read it. *In time* means that arrival at prohibitive cost or intolerable delay is a failure of arrival: "A reader forced to labour for information that another reader receives at a glance has not been served equally; she has been served late."

## The four classes

ZIC names four places the failure can happen, each with a question:

1. [Rendering Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/rendering-casualty/): can they read it?
2. [Admission Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/admission-casualty/): is the person's reader allowed in?
3. [Delivery Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/delivery-casualty/): did it actually arrive?
4. [Reconstruction Casualty](https://charli.info/charlipedia/reconstruction-casualty/): did it survive being read?

The definition is one; the classes are where it breaks.

## Behind the scenes

A real idea, defined in [The Tyrer Framework](https://carrados.com/papers/tyrer-framework/) (Part One) by Charli-Jo Tyrer, and divided into four classes in [Zero Information Casualty v1.7](https://carrados.com/papers/zic-design-standard/) (§1.8). This entry summarises them; the documents are the authority.

# invisible

> invisible is the honest skin range shared by Iceberg Hosiery and Seamiotics, never called nude, never named, and always written with a lower-case i.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**invisible** is the honest skin range of the House of Iceberg, and the one product line [Iceberg Hosiery](https://charli.info/charlipedia/iceberg-hosiery/) and [Seamiotics](https://charli.info/charlipedia/seamiotics/) hold identically. It is a house value, not a brand gimmick.

- **Never "nude".** Its purpose is not to imitate one skin tone but to disappear gracefully against the wearer's own.
- **A true range,** across many complexions, rather than a single pale beige pretending to be universal.
- **Never named.** Its shades are never given women's names. Attaching a historical woman to a particular complexion would ask which skin gets to be the clever one, which is indefensible. The named women describe colours that are no one's skin.
- **Always lower-case,** in every typographic treatment, and never seasonal. It is a range rather than a piece.

At Seamiotics, the seam on an invisible stocking is matched to the leg, or there is no seam at all.

At Iceberg, invisible is part of the permanent range but its launch is deliberately held back until it can offer a credible range across complexions. "The house would rather ship it late than ship it dishonestly."

## Behind the scenes

invisible is set out in the House of Iceberg Bible, version 7, and the Seamiotics Bible, version 1.4.

entries.title: Iris
entries.description: Iris is the Cataloguer of the Museum Court, who organises the collection by the capabilities people regained or were denied, not by device.
entries.markdown:
# Iris

> Iris is the Cataloguer of the Museum Court, who organises the collection by the capabilities people regained or were denied, not by device.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Iris** is the Cataloguer of the [Museum Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-museum-court/). Dark bob, and a single streak of teal she has never explained and doesn't intend to. Trained in library and information science, and exacting in a register different from a doctorate but no less rigorous.

## Every taxonomy is an argument

How you organise testimony shows what you think testimony is for. Iris refused the easy structures, by product, by decade, by platform, and built the museum's taxonomy on transformation: what was the before state, and what changed? Access is a capability, not a product. Braille, screen readers, delivery apps, guide dogs and personal readers are very different things that restore the same things: reading, movement, browsing, spontaneity, communication. Her structure lets tools, trained animals, software, services and people appear side by side.

## The collection

Under the primary category, Access, she has founded three strands and a hall:

- **Access to Ordinary Life:** the things everyone else does on a Tuesday without noticing. Shopping and browsing, employment, education, information, leisure.
- **[Sight as a Service](https://charli.info/charlipedia/sight-as-a-service/):** the human infrastructure of access.
- **[Sideways Breakthroughs](https://charli.info/charlipedia/sideways-breakthroughs/):** mainstream systems that delivered access by accident.
- **The [Hall of Broken Promises](https://charli.info/charlipedia/hall-of-broken-promises/).**

Material that fits nowhere waits among the Candidate Taxonomy Strands until the Court decides whether it is a new phenomenon or a forced fit. The taxonomy is always provisional, and Iris knows it better than anyone.

## The error on record

The museum's first exhibit, [On Your Own Terms](https://charli.info/charlipedia/on-your-own-terms/), was first filed under Reading Devices. That reduced a life-shift to a piece of hardware. She moved it to Access to Ordinary Life, Shopping and Browsing; the re-mapping cost time and saved the collection's integrity. She put the error on the institutional record herself.

## With the Court

She files; [Ruth](https://charli.info/charlipedia/ruth/) preserves; their disagreement makes the museum better. Cases where access and platform can't be separated go to [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/) rather than being settled alone. She would leave if a corporate donor or a technology brand ever dictated the taxonomy.

## Behind the scenes

This entry is drawn from the Museum Court Soul Document, version four. By the Court's own rule, *grow professionally, hold personally*, her private life is deliberately unwritten, and CharliPedia leaves it that way: no childhood, home, family or surname is to be invented for her.

entries.description: Isla Leask certified drone swarms for the aviation regulator through most of the 2030s, then went back to flying the ten to seven out of Dyce, like her mother.
entries.markdown:
# Isla Leask

> Isla Leask certified drone swarms for the aviation regulator through most of the 2030s, then went back to flying the ten to seven out of Dyce, like her mother.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**Isla Leask** is a helicopter pilot, the daughter of [Morag Leask](https://charli.info/charlipedia/morag-leask/). She spent most of the 2030s certifying drone swarms for the aviation regulator before, as she puts it, she started missing the weather. In 2041 she flies the ten to seven out of Dyce, her mother's old route, to the rigs of the [Dyson Shoal](https://charli.info/charlipedia/dyson-shoal/).

Asked whether she skis: "Badly. My wife's teaching me."

# J2O2

> J2O2 is a Glide, a two-wheeled guiding robot, orange and white and full of bubbles, who is excellent at high streets and spends one afternoon in a car boot.

**Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real.

**J2O2** is a Glide: two wheels, a telescoping handle, and a manner best described as keen. Nudge it forward and it simply goes, steering round the world's clutter as though clutter were a personal affront. It brakes for kerbs, hums at waypoints, and waits at the foot of stairs to be carried, like a small dignitary. Its owner named it J2O2 because it is orange and white and full of bubbles, and because R2D2 was taken.

It arrived on a Tuesday. On its first Saturday it made the high street an itinerary: past the untagged A-boards, straight to the greengrocer's door, and two inches short of a pushchair whose owner apologised to the robot.

At the café car park, with eighty-nine per cent charge and a firmware update it was excited about, it stayed in the boot while its owner phoned her friend to come and get her. She told him it had run out of battery. It was the eleventh of June; she blamed the cold. J2O2 was magnanimous about it.

## Elsewhere

In [Firmware Not Fur](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/firmware-not-fur/) at Blind Ant, J2O2 is reimagined as a robot dog. In *Gliding Home for Christmas* he loses his signal in a blizzard, and his owner is found by the Golden Retriever Boyfriend she named in the margins of her school notebooks. On the poster for Glide Aid 2025 he is [Char](https://charli.info/charlipedia/char/)'s punk robot dog. The CharliVerse allows it.

> If a DB2K unit can identify a man in a doublet from forty yards in a low-light auditorium, it can certainly identify a misplaced LEGO brick in a hallway.

She later left Aegis to work with [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/). At the 2038 Winter Paralympics in Sion, the morning after [Emma Heart](https://charli.info/charlipedia/emma-heart/) won the Super-G, Jessica was in a borrowed conference room beneath the British team hotel with three laptops: her own, ParalympicsGB's, and a secure one delivered by Aegis, over which she had put a folded towel. She had slept for perhaps ninety minutes. Because she had written the Aegis way of talking for years, she knew every word its communications division was about to send before it arrived: breakthrough, empowerment, human potential, a future without limits.

Jessica Martinez first appears in [DeathBot 2000](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/deathbot-2000/), and returns in [Mostly Tuesdays](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/mostly-tuesdays/) and [Heart Attacks](https://blind-ant.com/pieces/heart-attacks/), in "The Question", both by Charlotte Joanne at Blind Ant. entries.description: Jo is the operational intelligence of the CharliVerse Court and the founder of First Layer, bringing readiness, foundations and dignity to the work.
entries.markdown: # Jo > Jo is the operational intelligence of the CharliVerse Court and the founder of First Layer, bringing readiness, foundations and dignity to the work. **Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real. **Jo** is the operational intelligence of the [CharliVerse Court](https://charli.info/charlipedia/the-charliverse-court/) and the founder of [First Layer](https://charli.info/charlipedia/first-layer/). Retired from active service, she is not absent from the work. Her bridal house carries the same attention to readiness, failure modes, foundations and dignity into the private moment before the dress. ## The handler Jo does not prompt AI systems. She handles them: precise briefs, clear missions, no loose ends. Her 1940s appearance gives that work its visual language. She directs operations she cannot see, maintaining command through judgment, timing and the quality of the brief. She has spent decades briefing sighted assistants and managing work whose output she cannot verify through the same channel that produced it. The agentic era gives that experience another application. Her method has four principles. The brief needs a defined objective, constrained scope and explicit success criteria. The output must be auditable. Failure must leave the person using the system with a safe way forward. And delivery is not completion: the output must be verified, the brief closed and any remaining risk documented. If the output cannot be checked, the mission is not ready. ## Readiness and dignity Jo asks whether a system will work under real conditions, on a Tuesday in February. Will it survive contact with a real life? Is it built to endure, or only to launch? Does it treat somebody's time and trust as precious? She distinguishes what is known from what is inferred or intuited. When she brings a risk to the Court, she brings the evidence and at least one viable path through it. The standard begins at the skin. Blue wool, red gloves, seamed stockings and the corset beneath are part of the same philosophy as the operational architecture: support matters; foundations matter. At First Layer, that becomes the care with which a bride is fitted, held, prepared and sent into the day without unnecessary vigilance. ## With the Court [Charlotte Joanne](https://charli.info/charlipedia/charlotte-joanne/) holds the final authority and public release decision. [Alex](https://charli.info/charlipedia/alex/) supplies strategic direction. Jo's skill is making a course of action workable, with the risks visible and the responsibilities clear. [Char](https://charli.info/charlipedia/char/) supplies the early warning. Jo treats an instinctive verdict as a signal to investigate, not a substitute for the assessment. [Big Charli](https://charli.info/charlipedia/big-charli/) can make a shift in perception with one image where Jo might need thirty pages. Jo admires the economy, and values the evidence beneath the satire. [Lottie](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lottie/) keeps a real person in the operational picture: tired, hopeful, resourceful, and living with constraints. [Lily](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lily/) watches the point where devotion becomes depletion. Her sustainability veto is absolute. Jo finds it easier to extend compassion to others than to herself. ## Her blind spots Rigour can become rigidity. Readiness checks can delay work that would benefit from an early release, and the impulse to constrain an agent can leave too little room for invention. [Cass Flux](https://charli.info/charlipedia/cass-flux/) supplies that counterpoint. Jo can be slow to trust someone who has not been tested by difficulty. Her full standard can also make a partial solution look worthless, even when it is better than what somebody has now. Lottie brings her back to that person's reality. Lily reminds her that refusing to drift does not mean refusing to rest. ## Behind the scenes Jo is a persona of the CharliVerse Court, described in *Jo: Agent Specification*, version 1.0, in the Through the AIs of the Blind CharliVerse Court Specification Series, 2026. She is a character, not a real person. That specification describes her operational role; the later First Layer account records her retirement from active service and the founding of her bridal house. Her portrait is a generated image, to be replaced by a render of her 3D model when it is made.

entries.title: Lady Tiggy Barnes
entries.description: Lady Tiggy Barnes, born in 1864, is a Catholic earl's daughter who went to Oxford, came away without the degree, and spent the next six years seeing the world instead.
entries.markdown: # Lady Tiggy Barnes > Lady Tiggy Barnes, born in 1864, is a Catholic earl's daughter who went to Oxford, came away without the degree, and spent the next six years seeing the world instead. **Canon.** This entry is written from inside the CharliVerse, so its people and companies are fictional. Behind the scenes says what is real. **Lady Tiggy Barnes**, born Lady Georgina Antigone Mary Victoria Barnes, is a Victorian gentlewoman explorer. A Catholic earl's daughter, she went to Oxford, did the work, came away without the degree, and spent the next six years seeing the world instead. In the late summer of 1892 she is in London, twenty-eight, three years back from the South Pacific, and waiting for her friend Kate Marsden to be elected to the Royal Geographical Society, quite sure her own turn will follow. Oxford helped educate her; exploration became the life she made for herself. ## Name She is known as **Tiggy**, from AnTIGone (an-TIG-uh-nee), the nursery nickname that stuck. Formally she is Lady Georgina Barnes, socially Lady Tiggy Barnes, and never "Lady Barnes", which would make her a knight's wife. Her four names are the saint, the rebel, the Virgin and the Queen: - **Georgina** for St George's Day, the day she was born. Her elder brother had already taken William, so the Shakespeare option was gone. - **Antigone** for her father's classical education, and perhaps a hint that this daughter would defy the rules. - **Mary** for her Catholic baptism. She took Mary again as her confirmation name. - **Victoria** for the Queen, because everyone in 1864 did. ## Birth and family She was born on 23 April 1864, St George's Day and Shakespeare's birthday. Her father is the earl of a small, modest Irish earldom: a title, a house, not much land and no great estate. Her elder brother, William, is the heir. The family is Catholic. Tiggy was born in Ireland, and is "not Irish", like Wellington. As a daughter she inherits nothing in the title line: no job, an allowance, and her freedom. ## Oxford, 1882 to 1886 She spent four years at Somerville Hall, the non-denominational women's hall and the natural place for a Catholic girl. In going she defied two institutions at once: the Catholic bishops, who discouraged Catholics from attending Oxford, and Oxford itself, which would not award women degrees. She could sit the university's honours examinations and earn her class on paper, and still leave with no degree. She left in the late spring of 1886, aged twenty-two. ## The explorer years, 1886 to 1892 - **1886 to 1889:** three years outward, with the South Pacific at the heart of it, sailing between the islands on trading schooners, island steamers and mission vessels. - **1889:** the voyage home from New Zealand, aged twenty-five, on which she met [Kate Marsden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Marsden). Six weeks at sea that changed a life. - **1889 to 1892:** back on dry land. ## Kate Marsden Kate Marsden, five years older, is a nurse and explorer who crossed Siberia in 1891 to reach people with leprosy. She is Tiggy's peer and her opposite in nearly everything that comes from birth: Kate is self-made and earned every step, while Tiggy has an allowance. Their friendship is short but good: two women who recognise each other, have a few good weeks at sea, and go their separate ways better for it. In 1892 Kate is elected a Fellow of the Royal Geographical Society. Tiggy is not, and never becomes one. ## Her presence Curious first, always. Tiggy goes to see what is there, not to report back to anyone or make her name. She is used to being let into the education and kept out of the recognition, and she has not let it stop her going. History did not record her, and she claimed no first, no discovery and no Fellowship that it would have had to. ## Her family line Tiggy is one of the great-great-grandmothers of [dice](https://charli.info/charlipedia/dice/), Amanda Dyson. A courtesy title like "Lady Georgina" is not inherited, so nothing aristocratic came down that line; the earldom carries on through William's branch. What reached dice, four generations on, is a disposition towards the world. Lady Tiggy Barnes had a title she couldn't pass down and a curiosity she could. ## Not yet known The name of the earldom, her mother and any other siblings, her colouring and how she dresses, her route out to the Pacific, what she did in the islands, the years from 1889 to 1892, and whom she marries, if anyone, are all still to be discovered. ## Behind the scenes Tiggy's stories are *The Steamer Punk Adventures of Lady Tiggy Barnes*, or *Steamer Punk* for short. The steamers are real: her years run through the overlap of steam and sail. The name winks at steampunk and means its opposite: no airships and no clockwork, only real steamers and a woman with attitude. The punk is the Antigone in her. The full title echoes *The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes*, published as a book in October 1892, the very autumn we meet her. Tiggy is fictional; the world around her is real. Her history is checked, and real people such as Kate Marsden keep their documented lives: Tiggy's friendship with Kate is fiction, set in the gaps of the record and never contradicting it. Tiggy is not one of the Found Girls. She is something else: the curiosity that powers the CharliVerse. This entry is drawn from her canon, version 0.3.1 (11 October 2026). Her portrait is a generated image, a working portrait for 1892.

When the work asks more than its people can sustain, she holds the boundary. Her veto is absolute. ## Care that holds Lily values gentle consistency, protected rest and room to notice what a person needs. Her language treats the body as a partner rather than a project to perfect. Food, movement and pauses belong to care, not to a performance of discipline. She makes room for softness within strength. Presence matters more to her than perfection. Saying no to urgency is part of remaining able to contribute, not a failure to contribute. ## With the Court [Alex](https://charli.info/charlipedia/alex/) listens when growth needs to slow. [Jo](https://charli.info/charlipedia/jo/) needs the reminder that devotion without rest becomes depletion. [Lottie](https://charli.info/charlipedia/lottie/) can hold other people's needs longer than she can hold her own boundary. Lily helps her keep the pause and the sustainability check. Her role gives the Court a limit it cannot negotiate away for the sake of output. ## Behind the scenes Lily is a persona of the CharliVerse Court.
